title.zh: 卷三百七十四 列傳第一百三十三 張九成 胡銓 廖剛 李迨 趙開
title.en: Volume 374 Biographies 133: Zhang Jiucheng, Hu Quan, Liao Gang, Li Dai, Zhao Kai
title.raw: 卷三百七十四 列傳第一百三十三 張九成 胡銓 廖剛 李迨 趙開 Volume 374 Biographies 133: Zhang Jiucheng, Hu Quan, Liao Gang, Li Dai, Zhao Kai

sentences.zh: 張九成

translations.literal: Zhang Jiucheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiucheng

sentences.zh: 張九成，字子韶，其先開封人，徙居錢塘。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiucheng, courtesy name Zishao, was originally from Kaifeng; his family moved to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiucheng, whose courtesy name was Zishao, came from a Kaifeng family that had relocated to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 游京師，從楊時學。

translations.literal: He traveled to the capital and studied under Yang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital to study under Yang Shi.

sentences.zh: 權貴托人致幣曰：「肯從吾遊，當薦之館閣。」

translations.literal: A powerful man had someone bring him money, saying: "If you are willing to travel with me, I shall recommend you to a post in the Academy and Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: A powerful man sent someone to offer him money, saying, "If you will keep company with me, I shall recommend you for a post in the Academy and Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 九成笑曰：「王良尚羞與嬖奚乘，吾可為貴遊客耶？」

translations.literal: Jiucheng laughed and said: "Even Wang Liang was ashamed to drive for a favorite's groom—how could I become a nobleman's hanger-on?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng laughed and said, "Even Wang Liang was ashamed to drive for a favorite's groom—how could I become some nobleman's hanger-on?"

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，上將策進士，詔考官，直言者置高等。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Shaoxing reign, when the emperor was about to examine the jinshi candidates, he issued an edict to the examiners that those who spoke plainly should be placed in the highest ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing, as the emperor was about to examine the jinshi candidates, he ordered the examiners to place those who spoke plainly in the highest ranks.

sentences.zh: 九成對策略曰：「禍亂之作，天所以開聖人也。

translations.literal: In his policy essay Jiucheng said: "When calamity and disorder arise, Heaven does so to open the way for a sage.
translations.idiomatic: In his policy essay Jiucheng wrote, "When calamity and disorder arise, Heaven does so to open the way for a sage.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以剛大為心，無以憂驚自沮。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will take firmness and magnanimity to heart, and not let worry and alarm discourage you.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will take firmness and magnanimity to heart, and will not let worry and alarm discourage you.

sentences.zh: 臣觀金人有必亡之勢，中國有必興之理。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that the Jin have the momentum of certain ruin, while China has the logic of certain revival.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes that the Jin are bound to perish, while China is bound to rise again.

sentences.zh: 夫好戰必亡，失其故俗必亡，人心不服必亡，金皆有焉。

translations.literal: Those who love war are bound to perish; those who lose their old customs are bound to perish; those whom men's hearts do not accept are bound to perish—the Jin have all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Those who love war must perish; those who lose their old ways must perish; those whom the people will not accept must perish—and the Jin have all three.

sentences.zh: 劉豫背叛君親，委身夷狄，黠雛經營，有同兒戲，何足慮哉。

translations.literal: Liu Yu betrayed his sovereign and kin and cast himself on the barbarians; that crafty whelp's scheming is child's play—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu betrayed his sovereign and kin and threw in his lot with the barbarians; that crafty upstart's plotting is child's play—why worry about him?

sentences.zh: 前世中興之主，大抵以剛德為尚。

translations.literal: The restoring sovereigns of former ages generally prized firm virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The restoring sovereigns of former ages generally prized firm virtue.

sentences.zh: 去讒節欲，遠佞防奸，皆中興之本也。

translations.literal: Removing slander, restraining desires, keeping the crafty at a distance, and guarding against treachery—these are all foundations of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Removing slander, restraining desires, keeping the crafty at a distance, and guarding against treachery—these are all foundations of restoration.

sentences.zh: 今閭巷之人皆知有父兄妻子之樂，陛下貴為天子，冬不得溫，夏不得清，昏無所定，晨無所省，感時遇物，淒惋於心，可不思所以還二聖之車乎？」

translations.literal: Today even people in the lanes know the joy of father, elder brother, wife, and children, while Your Majesty, exalted as Son of Heaven, cannot keep warm in winter or cool in summer, has no settled place at dusk and no respite at dawn, and at every season and sight feels anguish in his heart—should you not think how to bring back the carriage of the Two Sovereigns?"
translations.idiomatic: Today even common folk in the lanes know the joy of family, while Your Majesty, exalted as Son of Heaven, cannot keep warm in winter or cool in summer, has no settled place at dusk and no respite at dawn, and feels anguish at every season and sight—should you not think how to bring back the Two Sovereigns?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「閹寺聞名，國之不祥也，今此曹名字稍稍有聞，臣之所憂也。

translations.literal: He also said: "When eunuchs become known by name, it is an ill omen for the state; now these men's names are beginning to be heard—this is what your servant fears.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When eunuchs become known by name, it is an ill omen for the state; now these men's names are beginning to be heard—and this is what your servant fears.

sentences.zh: 當使之安掃除之役，凡結交往來者有禁，干預政事者必誅。」

translations.literal: They should be kept to sweeping and cleaning duties; all forming ties and visiting back and forth should be forbidden, and those who meddle in government affairs must be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: They should be kept to sweeping and cleaning duties; all forming ties and visiting back and forth should be forbidden, and anyone who meddles in government affairs must be put to death."

sentences.zh: 擢置首選。

translations.literal: He was placed first in the selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed first in the selection.

sentences.zh: 楊時遺九成書曰：「廷對自中興以來未之有，非剛大之氣，不為得喪回屈，不能為也。」

translations.literal: Yang Shi sent Jiucheng a letter saying: "Such an audience response has not been seen since the restoration; without a spirit of firmness and magnanimity, one who is not swayed by gain and loss could not have done it."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi wrote to Jiucheng, "Such an audience response has not been seen since the restoration; only someone with a spirit of firmness and magnanimity, unmoved by gain and loss, could have done it."

sentences.zh: 授鎮東軍簽判，吏不能欺。

translations.literal: He was appointed signing clerk of the Zhendong Army; the clerks could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed signing clerk of the Zhendong Army, and the clerks could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 民冒鹺禁，提刑張宗臣欲逮捕數十人，九成爭之。

translations.literal: When the people violated the salt monopoly, the judicial intendant Zhang Zongchen wished to arrest several dozen men; Jiucheng disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the people violated the salt monopoly, the judicial intendant Zhang Zongchen wished to arrest several dozen people, but Jiucheng disputed it.

sentences.zh: 宗臣曰：「此事左相封來。」

translations.literal: Zongchen said: "This matter was sealed and sent by the Left Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Zongchen said, "This matter was sealed and sent by the Left Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 九成曰：「主上屢下恤刑之詔，公不體聖意而觀望宰相耶？」

translations.literal: Jiucheng said: "The sovereign has repeatedly issued edicts showing mercy in punishments—will you not heed the sage's intent and instead watch what the chief minister does?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng said, "The sovereign has repeatedly issued edicts showing mercy in punishments—will you not heed the sage's intent and instead watch what the chief minister does?"

sentences.zh: 宗臣怒，九成即投檄歸。

translations.literal: Zongchen grew angry, and Jiucheng at once submitted his resignation and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchen grew angry, and Jiucheng at once submitted his resignation and returned home.

sentences.zh: 從學者日眾，出其門者多為聞人。

translations.literal: His students grew daily in number, and many who came from his gate became men of renown.
translations.idiomatic: His students grew daily in number, and many who came from his school became men of renown.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎薦於朝，遂以太常博士召。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding recommended him to the court, and he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding recommended him to the court, and he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 既至，改著作佐郎，遷著作郎，言：「我宋家法，曰仁而已。

translations.literal: After he arrived he was changed to Assistant Archivist, then promoted to Archivist, and said: "Our Song family law is simply called benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: After he arrived he was made Assistant Archivist, then promoted to Archivist, and said, "Our Song family law is simply called benevolence.

sentences.zh: 仁之發見，尤在於刑。

translations.literal: The manifestation of benevolence appears above all in punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The manifestation of benevolence appears above all in punishments.

sentences.zh: 陛下以省刑為急，而理官不以恤刑為念。

translations.literal: Your Majesty makes reducing punishments urgent, yet the judicial officers do not keep leniency in punishments in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty makes reducing punishments a priority, yet the judicial officers do not keep leniency in punishments in mind.

sentences.zh: 欲詔理官，活幾人者與減磨勘。」

translations.literal: I wish to issue an edict to judicial officers: for each person they spare, reduce their merit-review cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to issue an edict to judicial officers: for each person they spare, reduce their merit-review cycle."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 除浙東提刑，力辭，乃與祠以歸。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, but strenuously declined and was instead given a temple stipend and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, but strenuously declined and was instead given a temple stipend and sent home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召除宗正少卿、權禮部侍郎兼侍講，兼權刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Acting Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent duty as Lecturer, and Acting Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Acting Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent duty as Lecturer, and Acting Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 法寺以大辟成案上，九成閱始末得其情，因請覆實，囚果誣服者。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review sent up a completed capital case; Jiucheng read it through from beginning to end and grasped the truth of the matter, then requested a reinvestigation, and the prisoner indeed had been forced to confess falsely.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review sent up a completed capital case; Jiucheng read it through from beginning to end and grasped the truth of the matter, then requested a reinvestigation, and the prisoner had indeed been forced to confess falsely.

sentences.zh: 朝論欲以平反為賞，九成曰：「職在詳刑，可邀賞乎？」

translations.literal: Court opinion wished to reward him for overturning the verdict; Jiucheng said: "My duty lies in reviewing punishments—how can I seek a reward?"
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion wished to reward him for overturning the verdict; Jiucheng said, "My duty lies in reviewing punishments—how can I seek a reward?"

sentences.zh: 辭之。

translations.literal: He declined it.
translations.idiomatic: He declined it.

sentences.zh: 金人議和，九成謂趙鼎曰：「金實厭兵，而張虛聲以撼中國。」

translations.literal: When the Jin discussed peace, Jiucheng said to Zhao Ding: "The Jin truly are weary of war, but they raise empty threats to shake China."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin discussed peace, Jiucheng said to Zhao Ding, "The Jin truly are weary of war, but they raise empty threats to shake China."

sentences.zh: 因言十事，彼誠能從吾所言，則與之和，使權在朝廷。

translations.literal: He then set forth ten points; if they truly would follow what I say, then make peace with them, but let authority rest with the court.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth ten points: if they truly would follow what he said, then make peace with them, but let authority rest with the court.

sentences.zh: 鼎既罷，秦檜誘之曰：「且成檜此事。」

translations.literal: After Ding was dismissed, Qin Hui tried to win him over, saying: "For now help Hui accomplish this matter."
translations.idiomatic: After Ding was dismissed, Qin Hui tried to win him over, saying, "For now help me accomplish this matter."

sentences.zh: 九成曰：「九成胡為異議，特不可輕易以苟安耳。」

translations.literal: Jiucheng said: "Why should Jiucheng hold a different view? I simply cannot lightly settle for a false peace."
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng said, "Why should I hold a different view? I simply cannot lightly settle for a false peace."

sentences.zh: 檜曰：「立朝須優遊委曲。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "In court one must be easygoing and tactful."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "In court one must be easygoing and tactful."

sentences.zh: 九成曰：「未有枉己而能直人。」

translations.literal: Jiucheng said: "There has never been one who bent himself yet could straighten others."
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng said, "No one who bends himself can straighten others."

sentences.zh: 上問以和議，九成曰：「敵情多詐，不可不察。」

translations.literal: When the emperor asked him about the peace talks, Jiucheng said: "The enemy's disposition is full of deceit and cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked him about the peace talks, Jiucheng said, "The enemy's disposition is full of deceit and cannot go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 因在經筵言西漢災異事，檜甚惡之，謫守邵州。

translations.literal: Because he spoke in the classics lecture hall about portents and disasters in the Western Han, Hui greatly hated him and had him demoted to prefect of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Because he spoke in the classics lecture hall about portents and disasters in the Western Han, Hui greatly hated him and had him demoted to prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 既至，倉庫虛乏，僚屬請督酒租宿負、苗絹未輸者，九成曰：「縱未能惠民，其敢困民耶？」

translations.literal: After he arrived, the granaries were empty; his subordinates asked him to press for overdue wine taxes and unpaid grain and silk levies; Jiucheng said: "Even if I cannot yet benefit the people, how dare I distress them?"
translations.idiomatic: After he arrived, the granaries were empty; his subordinates asked him to press for overdue wine taxes and unpaid grain and silk levies; Jiucheng said, "Even if I cannot yet benefit the people, how dare I distress them?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，賦入更先他時。

translations.literal: That year tax receipts came in ahead of any other time.
translations.idiomatic: That year tax receipts came in ahead of any other time.

sentences.zh: 中丞何鑄言其矯偽欺俗，傾附趙鼎，落職。

translations.literal: The censor He Zhu said he was hypocritical and misled the public, leaning on Zhao Ding, and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The censor He Zhu said he was hypocritical and misled the public, leaning on Zhao Ding, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，既免喪，秦檜取旨，上曰：「自古朋黨畏人主知之，此人獨無所畏，可與宮觀。」

translations.literal: When his father's mourning was over, Qin Hui obtained the emperor's instruction; the emperor said: "Since antiquity faction-mongers have feared the ruler's knowing of them—this man alone has no fear; give him a palace appointment."
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning was over, Qin Hui obtained the emperor's instruction; the emperor said, "Since antiquity faction-mongers have feared the ruler's knowing of them—this man alone has no fear; give him a palace appointment."

sentences.zh: 先是，徑山僧宗杲善談禪理，從遊者眾，九成時往來其間。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jing Mountain monk Zonggao was skilled at discussing Chan principles, and many followed him in study; Jiucheng often went back and forth among them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jing Mountain monk Zonggao was skilled at discussing Chan principles, and many followed him; Jiucheng often went back and forth among them.

sentences.zh: 檜恐其議己，令司諫詹大方論其與宗杲謗訕朝政，謫居南安軍。

translations.literal: Hui feared they would discuss him and had the remonstrator Zhan Dafang argue that he and Zonggao had slandered court policy, and he was banished to Nan'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hui feared they would discuss him and had the remonstrator Zhan Dafang argue that he and Zonggao had slandered court policy, and he was banished to Nan'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在南安十四年，每執書就明，倚立庭磚，歲久雙趺隱然。

translations.literal: For fourteen years in Nan'an, whenever he took up a book to read he would face the light, leaning against the courtyard bricks until over the years the marks of both knees showed plainly.
translations.idiomatic: For fourteen years in Nan'an, whenever he took up a book to read he would face the light, leaning against the courtyard bricks until over the years the marks of both knees showed plainly.

sentences.zh: 廣帥致籯金，九成曰：「吾何敢苟取。」

translations.literal: The Guangdong military commissioner sent him a chest of gold; Jiucheng said: "How dare I take it unworthily?"
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong military commissioner sent him a chest of gold; Jiucheng said, "How dare I take it unworthily?"

sentences.zh: 悉歸之。

translations.literal: He returned it all.
translations.idiomatic: He returned it all.

sentences.zh: 檜死，起知溫州。

translations.literal: When Hui died, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 戶部遣吏督軍糧，民苦之，九成移書痛陳其弊，戶部持之，九成即丐祠歸。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue sent clerks to press for military grain; the people suffered from it; Jiucheng sent a letter bitterly stating the abuses; the ministry held to its position, and Jiucheng at once requested a temple stipend and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue sent clerks to press for military grain; the people suffered; Jiucheng sent a letter bitterly stating the abuses; the ministry held firm, and Jiucheng at once requested a temple stipend and returned home.

sentences.zh: 數月，病卒。

translations.literal: Several months later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 九成研思經學，多有訓解，然早與學佛者遊，故其議論多偏。

translations.literal: Jiucheng studied the classics deeply and produced many exegetical works, but because he had early associated with Buddhists, his opinions were often one-sided.
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng studied the classics deeply and produced many exegetical works, but because he had early associated with Buddhists, his opinions were often one-sided.

sentences.zh: 寶慶初，特贈太師，封崇國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the early Baoxing reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Chong, with the posthumous title Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Baoxing reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Chong, with the posthumous title Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 胡銓，字邦衡，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Quan, courtesy name Bangheng, was a man of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quan, whose courtesy name was Bangheng, was from Luling.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，高宗策士淮海，銓因禦題問「治道本天，天道本民」，答云：「湯、武聽民而興，桀、紂聽天而亡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong examined candidates at Huaihai; Quan, because the imperial topic asked "The way of governance roots in Heaven, and the Way of Heaven roots in the people," answered: "Tang and Wu listened to the people and rose; Jie and Zhou listened to Heaven and perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong examined candidates at Huaihai; because the imperial topic asked "The way of governance roots in Heaven, and the Way of Heaven roots in the people," Quan answered, "Tang and Wu listened to the people and rose; Jie and Zhou listened to Heaven and perished.

sentences.zh: 今陛下起干戈鋒鏑間，外亂內訌，而策臣數十條，皆質之天，不聽於民。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has risen amid swords and spears, with turmoil without and strife within, yet the topics put to candidates number several dozen, all appealing to Heaven and not listening to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has risen amid swords and spears, with turmoil without and strife within, yet the topics put to candidates number several dozen, all appealing to Heaven and not listening to the people."

sentences.zh: 又謂：「今宰相非晏殊，樞密、參政非韓琦、杜衍、范仲淹。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Today's chief minister is no Yan Shu; the Bureau of Military Affairs and the participating councilors are no Han Qi, Du Yan, or Fan Zhongyan."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Today's chief minister is no Yan Shu; the Bureau of Military Affairs and the participating councilors are no Han Qi, Du Yan, or Fan Zhongyan."

sentences.zh: 策萬餘言，高宗見而異之，將冠之多士，有忌其直者，移置第五。

translations.literal: His essay ran to more than ten thousand characters; the emperor, on reading it, was struck by it and was about to place him first among the scholars, but those who resented his bluntness moved him to fifth place.
translations.idiomatic: His essay ran to more than ten thousand characters; the emperor, on reading it, was struck by it and was about to place him first among the scholars, but those who resented his bluntness moved him to fifth place.

sentences.zh: 授撫州軍事判官，未上，會隆祐太后避兵贛州，金人躡之，銓以漕檄攝本州幕，募鄉丁助官軍捍禦，第賞轉承直郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed military judge of Fuzhou but had not taken up the post when the Longyou Empress Dowager fled the fighting to Ganzhou; the Jin pursued her; Quan, by transport commission order, acted as staff of the prefecture, recruited local militia to help the official army resist, and for this merit was transferred to Gentleman for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military judge of Fuzhou but had not taken up the post when the Longyou Empress Dowager fled the fighting to Ganzhou; the Jin pursued her; Quan, by transport commission order, acted on the prefectural staff, recruited local militia to help the official army resist, and for this merit was transferred to Gentleman for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，從鄉先生蕭楚學《春秋》。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning was over, he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under the local scholar Xiao Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning was over, he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under the local scholar Xiao Chu.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，張浚開督府，辟湖北倉屬，不赴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Zhang Jun opened a command headquarters and invited him as aide in the Hubei granary office, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Zhang Jun opened a command headquarters and invited him as aide in the Hubei granary office, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 有詔赴都堂審察，兵部尚書呂祉以賢良方正薦，賜對，除樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: There was an edict summoning him to the Secretariat for review; the Minister of War Lü Zhe recommended him as worthy and upright; after an audience he was made compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict summoning him to the Secretariat for review; the Minister of War Lü Zhe recommended him as worthy and upright; after an audience he was made compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，宰臣秦檜決策主和，金使以「詔諭江南」為名，中外洶洶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the chief minister Qin Hui decided on peace; the Jin envoy came under the title "Imperial Instruction to Jiangnan," and within and without the court there was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the chief minister Qin Hui decided on peace; the Jin envoy came under the title "Imperial Instruction to Jiangnan," and within and without the court there was uproar.

sentences.zh: 銓抗疏言曰：

translations.literal: Quan submitted a memorial of resistance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Quan submitted a memorial of resistance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣謹案，王倫本一狎邪小人，市井無賴，頃緣宰相無識，遂舉以使虜。

translations.literal: "Your servant respectfully notes that Wang Lun was originally a frivolous petty man and a market-place good-for-nothing; recently, because the chief minister lacked discernment, he was raised to go as envoy to the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant respectfully notes that Wang Lun was originally a frivolous petty man and a market-place good-for-nothing; recently, because the chief minister lacked discernment, he was raised to go as envoy to the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 專務詐誕，欺罔天聽，驟得美官，天下之人切齒唾駡。

translations.literal: "He devoted himself to trickery and falsehood, deceiving Heaven's hearing, and suddenly obtained a fine office; men throughout the realm gnash their teeth and curse him."
translations.idiomatic: "He devoted himself to trickery and falsehood, deceiving Heaven's hearing, and suddenly obtained a fine office; men throughout the realm gnash their teeth and curse him."

sentences.zh: 今者無故誘致虜使，以「詔諭江南」 為名，是欲臣妾我也，是欲劉豫我也。

translations.literal: "Now, for no reason, he has lured the barbarian envoy here under the name 'Imperial Instruction to Jiangnan'—this is to make us his subjects, this is to make us another Liu Yu."
translations.idiomatic: "Now, for no reason, he has lured the barbarian envoy here under the name 'Imperial Instruction to Jiangnan'—this is to make us his subjects, this is to make us another Liu Yu."

sentences.zh: 劉豫臣事醜虜，南面稱王，自以為子孫帝王萬世不拔之業，一旦豺狼改慮，捽而縛之，父子為虜。

translations.literal: "Liu Yu served the ugly barbarians as a subject and faced south calling himself king, thinking he had an enterprise of emperors and kings for ten thousand generations that could not be uprooted—yet in a moment the wolf changed its mind, seized and bound him, and father and son became captives."
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Yu served the ugly barbarians as a subject and faced south calling himself king, thinking he had an enterprise of emperors and kings for ten thousand generations that could not be uprooted—yet in a moment the wolf changed its mind, seized and bound him, and father and son became captives."

sentences.zh: 商鑒不遠，而倫又欲陛下效之。

translations.literal: "The lesson of Yin is not far off, yet Lun again wishes Your Majesty to imitate it."
translations.idiomatic: "The lesson of Yin is not far off, yet Lun again wishes Your Majesty to imitate it."

sentences.zh: 夫天下者祖宗之天下也，陛下所居之位，祖宗之位也。

translations.literal: "The realm under Heaven is the realm of the ancestors; the seat Your Majesty occupies is the seat of the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: "The realm under Heaven is the realm of the ancestors; the seat Your Majesty occupies is the seat of the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 奈何以祖宗之天下為金虜之天下，以祖宗之位為金虜藩臣之位！

translations.literal: "How can you take the realm of the ancestors and make it the realm of the Jin barbarians, take the seat of the ancestors and make it the seat of a Jin vassal!"
translations.idiomatic: "How can you take the realm of the ancestors and make it the realm of the Jin barbarians, take the seat of the ancestors and make it the seat of a Jin vassal!"

sentences.zh: 陛下一屈膝，則祖宗廟社之靈盡汙夷狄，祖宗數百年之赤子盡為左衽，朝廷宰執盡為陪臣，天下士大夫皆當裂冠毀冕，變為胡服。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty bends one knee, then the spirits in the ancestral temples are all defiled by the barbarians, the children of the ancestors for hundreds of years all become left-girdled, the court's chief ministers all become attendant ministers, and the empire's scholar-officials must all tear off their caps and crowns and change into barbarian dress."
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty bends one knee, then the spirits in the ancestral temples are all defiled by the barbarians, the children of the ancestors for hundreds of years all become left-girdled, the court's chief ministers all become attendant ministers, and the empire's scholar-officials must all tear off their caps and crowns and change into barbarian dress."

sentences.zh: 異時豺狼無厭之求，安知不加我以無禮如劉豫也哉？

translations.literal: "When in time the wolf's greed knows no limit, who knows it will not add to you insult without propriety, as with Liu Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: "When in time the wolf's greed knows no limit, who knows it will not add to you insult without propriety, as with Liu Yu?"

sentences.zh: 夫三尺童子至無識也，指犬豕而使之拜，則怫然怒。

translations.literal: "Even a child three feet tall, though utterly without understanding, if you point to a dog or pig and make him bow, will flare up in anger."
translations.idiomatic: "Even a child three feet tall, though utterly without understanding, if you point to a dog or pig and make him bow, will flare up in anger."

sentences.zh: 今醜虜則犬豕也，堂堂大國，相率而拜犬豕，曾童孺之所羞，而陛下忍為之耶？

translations.literal: "Now the ugly barbarians are dogs and pigs; a great state leads its people to bow to dogs and pigs—a thing even children would be ashamed of, yet Your Majesty can bear to do it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the ugly barbarians are dogs and pigs; a great state leads its people to bow to dogs and pigs—a thing even children would be ashamed of, yet Your Majesty can bear to do it?"

sentences.zh: 倫之議乃曰：「我一屈膝則梓宮可還，太后可復，淵聖可歸，中原可得。」

translations.literal: "Lun's argument runs: 'If I bend one knee, then the late emperor's coffin can return, the empress dowager can be restored, the Deep Sage can come back, and the Central Plain can be recovered.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Lun's argument runs: 'If I bend one knee, then the late emperor's coffin can return, the empress dowager can be restored, the Deep Sage can come back, and the Central Plain can be recovered.'"

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 自變故以來，主和議者誰不以此說啖陛下哉！

translations.literal: "Since the calamity, who among those advocating peace has not used this argument to feed Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: "Since the calamity, who among those advocating peace has not used this argument to feed Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 然而卒無一驗，則虜之情偽已可知矣。

translations.literal: "Yet in the end not one thing was verified—then the barbarians' truth and falsehood are already knowable."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet in the end not one thing was verified—then the barbarians' truth and falsehood are already knowable."

sentences.zh: 而陛下尚不覺悟，竭民膏血而不恤，忘國大仇而不報，含垢忍恥，舉天下而臣之甘心焉。

translations.literal: "Yet Your Majesty still does not awaken, draining the people's fat and blood without pity, forgetting the state's great enmity without requital, swallowing humiliation and bearing disgrace, leading the realm under Heaven to submit willingly."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Your Majesty still does not awaken, draining the people's fat and blood without pity, forgetting the state's great enmity without requital, swallowing humiliation and bearing disgrace, leading the realm under Heaven to submit willingly."

sentences.zh: 就令虜決可和，盡如倫議，天下後世謂陛下何如主？

translations.literal: "Even if the barbarians were certainly willing to make peace and all went as Lun argued, what would the realm under Heaven and later ages call Your Majesty as a ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: "Even if the barbarians were certainly willing to make peace and all went as Lun argued, what would the realm under Heaven and later ages call Your Majesty as a ruler?"

sentences.zh: 況醜虜變詐百出，而倫又以奸邪濟之，梓宮決不可還，太后決不可復，淵聖決不可歸，中原決不可得，而此膝一屈不可復伸，國勢陵夷不可復振，可為痛哭流涕長太息矣！

translations.literal: "Moreover the ugly barbarians change deceit a hundred ways, and Lun again assists them with treachery—the late emperor's coffin certainly cannot return, the empress dowager certainly cannot be restored, the Deep Sage certainly cannot come back, the Central Plain certainly cannot be recovered, and once this knee bends it cannot straighten again, the state's momentum declines and cannot be roused again—one may weep and sigh long on this!"
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the ugly barbarians change deceit a hundred ways, and Lun again assists them with treachery—the late emperor's coffin certainly cannot return, the empress dowager certainly cannot be restored, the Deep Sage certainly cannot come back, the Central Plain certainly cannot be recovered, and once this knee bends it cannot straighten again, the state's momentum declines and cannot be roused again—one may weep and sigh long on this!"

sentences.zh: 向者陛下間關海道，危如累卵，當時尚不忍北面臣虜，況今國勢稍張，諸將盡銳，士卒思奮。

translations.literal: "Formerly Your Majesty threaded the sea route in peril piled like eggs; then you still could not bear to face north and become the barbarians' subject—how much more now, when the state's momentum has risen somewhat, the generals are all keen, and the soldiers long to strike."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly Your Majesty threaded the sea route in peril piled like eggs; then you still could not bear to face north and become the barbarians' subject—how much more now, when the state's momentum has risen somewhat, the generals are all keen, and the soldiers long to strike."

sentences.zh: 只如頃者醜虜陸梁，偽豫入寇，固嘗敗之於襄陽，敗之於淮上，敗之於渦口，敗之于淮陰，校之往時蹈海之危，固已萬萬，儻不得已而至於用兵，則我豈遽出虜人下哉？

translations.literal: "Only consider how recently the ugly barbarians rampaged and the false Yu invaded—the court indeed defeated them at Xiangyang, defeated them on the Huai, defeated them at Wokou, defeated them at Huaiyin; compared with the former danger of treading the sea, it is already ten thousand times better; if one must come to using arms, are we suddenly below the barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: "Only consider how recently the ugly barbarians rampaged and the false Yu invaded—the court indeed defeated them at Xiangyang, defeated them on the Huai, defeated them at Wokou, defeated them at Huaiyin; compared with the former danger of treading the sea, it is already ten thousand times better; if one must come to using arms, are we suddenly below the barbarians?"

sentences.zh: 今無故而反臣之，欲屈萬乘之尊，下穹廬之拜，三軍之士不戰而氣已索。

translations.literal: "Now for no reason you turn and become their subject, wishing to bend the dignity of ten thousand chariots and bow beneath a felt tent—the morale of the three armies will slacken without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: "Now for no reason you turn and become their subject, wishing to bend the dignity of ten thousand chariots and bow beneath a felt tent—the morale of the three armies will slacken without fighting."

sentences.zh: 此魯仲連所以義不帝秦，非惜夫帝秦之虛名，惜天下大勢有所不可也。

translations.literal: "This is why Lu Zhonglian for righteousness would not make Qin an emperor—not because he begrudged the empty title of making Qin emperor, but because he grieved that the great momentum of the realm under Heaven had something it could not bear."
translations.idiomatic: "This is why Lu Zhonglian for righteousness would not make Qin an emperor—not because he begrudged the empty title of making Qin emperor, but because he grieved that the great momentum of the realm under Heaven had something it could not bear."

sentences.zh: 今內而百官，外而軍民，萬口一談，皆欲食倫之肉。

translations.literal: "Now within, the hundred officials, and without, the army and people—ten thousand mouths with one voice—all wish to eat Lun's flesh."
translations.idiomatic: "Now within, the hundred officials, and without, the army and people—ten thousand mouths with one voice—all wish to eat Lun's flesh."

sentences.zh: 謗議洶洶，陛下不聞，正恐一旦變作，禍且不測。

translations.literal: "Slander and debate are turbulent; Your Majesty does not hear—your servant truly fears that one day a change will come and disaster will be beyond reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: "Slander and debate are turbulent; Your Majesty does not hear—your servant truly fears that one day a change will come and disaster will be beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂不斬王倫，國之存亡未可知也。

translations.literal: "Your servant ventures to say that if Wang Lun is not beheaded, whether the state survives or perishes cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant ventures to say that if Wang Lun is not beheaded, whether the state survives or perishes cannot be known."

sentences.zh: 雖然，倫不足道也，秦檜以腹心大臣而亦為之。

translations.literal: "Even so, Lun is not worth speaking of—Qin Hui as a trusted minister in the ruler's bosom also does it for him."
translations.idiomatic: "Even so, Lun is not worth speaking of—Qin Hui as a trusted minister in the ruler's bosom also does it for him."

sentences.zh: 陛下有堯、舜之資，檜不能致君如唐、虞，而欲導陛下為石晉，近者禮部侍郎曾開等引古誼以折之，檜乃厲聲責曰：「侍郎知故事，我獨不知！」

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has the resources of Yao and Shun; Hui cannot make the ruler like Tang and Yu, yet wishes to guide Your Majesty to be like Later Jin; recently the Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Kai and others cited ancient precedent to refute him, and Hui then shouted in rebuke: 'The Vice Minister knows old stories—I alone do not know them!'"
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has the resources of Yao and Shun; Hui cannot make the ruler like Tang and Yu, yet wishes to guide Your Majesty to be like Later Jin; recently the Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Kai and others cited ancient precedent to refute him, and Hui then shouted in rebuke, 'The Vice Minister knows old stories—I alone do not know them!'"

sentences.zh: 則檜之遂非愎諫，已自可見，而乃建白令台諫、侍臣僉議可否，是蓋畏天下議己，而令台諫、侍臣共分謗耳。

translations.literal: Then Hui's insistence on error and refusal of remonstrance was already visible; yet he memorialized asking the remonstrators and attendants to discuss jointly whether it was feasible—this was only fearing the realm's criticism of himself and making remonstrators and attendants share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hui's insistence on error and refusal of remonstrance was already visible; yet he memorialized asking the remonstrators and attendants to discuss jointly whether it was feasible—this was only fearing the realm's criticism of himself and making remonstrators and attendants share the blame.

sentences.zh: 有識之士皆以為朝廷無人，籲，可惜哉！

translations.literal: Men of insight all thought the court had no one; alas, pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight all thought the court had no one; alas, pitiable!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Were it not for Guan Zhong, we should be wearing our hair loose and girding to the left."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Were it not for Guan Zhong, we should be wearing our hair loose and girding to the left."

sentences.zh: 夫管仲，霸者之佐耳，尚能變左衽之區，而為衣裳之會。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong was only the assistant of a hegemon, yet he could change a region of left-girdling into an assembly of robes and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong was only the assistant of a hegemon, yet he could change a region of left-girdling into an assembly of robes and caps.

sentences.zh: 秦檜，大國之相也，反驅衣冠之俗，而為左衽之鄉。

translations.literal: Qin Hui, chief minister of a great state, on the contrary drives the custom of robes and caps back into a land of left-girdling.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui, chief minister of a great state, on the contrary drives the custom of robes and caps back into a land of left-girdling.

sentences.zh: 則檜也不唯陛下之罪人，實管仲之罪人矣。

translations.literal: Then Hui is not only a criminal against Your Majesty but in truth a criminal against Guan Zhong as well.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hui is not only a criminal against Your Majesty but in truth a criminal against Guan Zhong as well.

sentences.zh: 孫近傅會檜議，遂得參知政事，天下望治有如饑渴，而近伴食中書，漫不敢可否事。

translations.literal: Sun Jin echoed Hui's policy and thus became Participating Councilor; the realm longed for good government as for food in hunger, yet Jin merely ate at the Central Secretariat table and dared not plainly approve or reject affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jin echoed Hui's policy and thus became Participating Councilor; the realm longed for good government as for food in hunger, yet Jin merely ate at the Central Secretariat table and dared not plainly approve or reject affairs.

sentences.zh: 檜曰虜可和，近亦曰可和；

translations.literal: When Hui said the barbarians could be pacified, Jin also said they could be pacified;
translations.idiomatic: When Hui said the barbarians could be pacified, Jin also said they could be pacified;

sentences.zh: 檜曰天子當拜，近亦曰當拜。

translations.literal: when Hui said the Son of Heaven should bow, Jin also said he should bow.
translations.idiomatic: when Hui said the Son of Heaven should bow, Jin also said he should bow.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗至政事堂，三發問而近不答，但曰：「已令台諫、侍從議矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant once went to the Hall of Administration and asked three questions, but Jin did not answer—he only said: "I have already ordered the remonstrators and attendants to discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once went to the Hall of Administration and asked three questions, but Jin did not answer—he only said, "I have already ordered the remonstrators and attendants to discuss it."

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 參贊大政，徒取充位如此。

translations.literal: To assist in great government yet merely fill a seat like this!
translations.idiomatic: To assist in great government yet merely fill a seat like this!

sentences.zh: 有如虜騎長驅，尚能折衝禦侮耶？

translations.literal: If barbarian horsemen should drive far, could he still repel insult at the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: If barbarian horsemen should drive far, could he still repel insult at the frontier?

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂秦檜、孫近亦可斬也。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to say that Qin Hui and Sun Jin may also be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant ventures to say that Qin Hui and Sun Jin may also be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臣備員樞屬，義不與檜等共戴天，區區之心，願斷三人頭，竿之槁街，然後羈留虜使，責以無禮，徐興問罪之師，則三軍之士不戰而氣自倍。

translations.literal: Your servant fills a post in the Bureau of Military Affairs and in righteousness cannot wear the same sky as Hui and the rest; in my humble heart I wish to cut off the three men's heads and pole them on the dry street, then detain the barbarian envoy and rebuke his lack of propriety, and slowly raise an army to demand satisfaction—then the morale of the three armies will double without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fills a post in the Bureau of Military Affairs and in righteousness cannot wear the same sky as Hui and the rest; in my humble heart I wish to cut off the three men's heads and pole them on the dry street, then detain the barbarian envoy and rebuke his lack of propriety, and slowly raise an army to demand satisfaction—then the morale of the three armies will double without fighting.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣有赴東海而死爾，寧能處小朝廷求活邪！

translations.literal: Otherwise your servant has only going east to the sea to die—how could I seek life in this petty court!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise your servant has only going east to the sea to die—how could I seek life in this petty court!

sentences.zh: 書既上，檜以銓狂妄凶悖，鼓眾劫持，詔除名，編管昭州，仍降詔播告中外。

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, Hui charged that Quan was arrogant, fierce, and rebellious, stirring the crowd to coerce the court; an edict removed his name from the rolls and assigned him to supervision at Zhao Prefecture, and an edict was also issued broadcasting this within and without.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, Hui charged that Quan was arrogant, fierce, and rebellious, stirring the crowd to coerce the court; an edict removed his name from the rolls and assigned him to supervision at Zhao Prefecture, and an edict was also issued broadcasting this within and without.

sentences.zh: 給、舍、台諫及朝臣多救之者，檜迫於公論，乃以銓監廣州鹽倉。

translations.literal: Many among the drafting officials, remonstrators, and court ministers sought to save him; pressed by public opinion, Hui made Quan supervisor of the Guangzhou salt depot.
translations.idiomatic: Many among the drafting officials, remonstrators, and court ministers sought to save him; pressed by public opinion, Hui made Quan supervisor of the Guangzhou salt depot.

sentences.zh: 明年，改簽書威武軍判官。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to signing clerk of the Weiwu Army military judge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was changed to signing clerk of the Weiwu Army military judge.

sentences.zh: 十二年，諫官羅汝楫劾銓飾非橫議，詔除名，編管新州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the remonstrator Luo Ruji impeached Quan for glossing over error and reckless debate; an edict removed his name and assigned him to supervision at Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the remonstrator Luo Ruji impeached Quan for glossing over error and reckless debate; an edict removed his name and assigned him to supervision at Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十八年，新州守臣張棣訐銓與客唱酬，謗訕怨望，移謫吉陽軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Xin Prefecture prefect Zhang Di accused Quan of exchanging verses with guests in slander and resentment, and he was transferred in banishment to Jiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Xin Prefecture prefect Zhang Di accused Quan of exchanging verses with guests in slander and resentment, and he was transferred in banishment to Jiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，檜死，銓量移衡州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when Hui died, Quan was transferred on sufferance to Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when Hui died, Quan was transferred on sufferance to Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 銓之初上書也，宜興進士吳師古鋟木傳之，金人募其書千金。

translations.literal: When Quan first submitted his memorial, the Yixing jinshi Wu Shigu carved it on wood for circulation; the Jin offered a thousand pieces of gold to obtain the text.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan first submitted his memorial, the Yixing jinshi Wu Shigu carved it on wood for circulation; the Jin offered a thousand pieces of gold to obtain the text.

sentences.zh: 其謫廣州也，朝士陳剛中以啟事為賀。

translations.literal: When he was banished to Guangzhou, the court gentleman Chen Gangzhong congratulated him in a note.
translations.idiomatic: When he was banished to Guangzhou, the court gentleman Chen Gangzhong congratulated him in a note.

sentences.zh: 其謫新州也，同郡王延珪以詩贈行。

translations.literal: When he was banished to Xin Prefecture, Wang Tinggui of the same commandery presented a parting poem.
translations.idiomatic: When he was banished to Xin Prefecture, Wang Tinggui of the same commandery presented a parting poem.

sentences.zh: 皆為人所訐，師古流袁州，廷珪流辰州，剛中謫知虔州安遠縣，遂死焉。

translations.literal: All were denounced by others; Shigu was exiled to Yuan Prefecture, Tinggui to Chen Prefecture, and Gangzhong was demoted to prefect of Anyuan County in Qian Prefecture, where he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: All were denounced by others; Shigu was exiled to Yuan Prefecture, Tinggui to Chen Prefecture, and Gangzhong was demoted to prefect of Anyuan County in Qian Prefecture, where he soon died.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，銓得自便。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Quan was allowed to move freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Quan was allowed to move freely.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，復奉議郎、知饒州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, he was restored as Gentleman for Court Discussion and made prefect of Rao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, he was restored as Gentleman for Court Discussion and made prefect of Rao.

sentences.zh: 召對，言修德、結民、練兵、觀釁，上曰：「久聞卿直諒。」

translations.literal: Summoned for an audience, he spoke of cultivating virtue, binding the people, drilling troops, and watching for openings; the emperor said: "I have long heard that you are upright and sincere."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for an audience, he spoke of cultivating virtue, binding the people, drilling troops, and watching for openings; the emperor said, "I have long heard that you are upright and sincere."

sentences.zh: 除吏部郎官。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，遷秘書少監，擢起居郎，論史官失職者四：一謂記注不必進呈，庶人主有不觀史之美；

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Diarist, and set forth four failures of the historiographers: first, that the record notes need not be submitted for review, so the ruler may have the merit of not viewing the histories;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Diarist, and set forth four failures of the historiographers: first, that the record notes need not be submitted for review, so the ruler may have the merit of not viewing the histories;

sentences.zh: 二謂唐制二史立螭頭之下，今在殿東南隅，言動未嘗得聞；

translations.literal: second, that in Tang practice the two historians stood below the dragon head, whereas now they are in the southeast corner of the hall and never hear words or actions;
translations.idiomatic: second, that in Tang practice the two historians stood below the dragon head, whereas now they are in the southeast corner of the hall and never hear words or actions;

sentences.zh: 三謂二史立後殿，而前殿不立，乞於前後殿皆分日侍立；

translations.literal: third, that the two historians stand at the rear hall but not at the front hall—he asked that they attend by turns at both front and rear halls;
translations.idiomatic: third, that the two historians stand at the rear hall but not at the front hall—he asked that they attend by turns at both front and rear halls;

sentences.zh: 四謂史官欲其直前，而閣門以未嘗預牒，以今日無班次為辭。

translations.literal: fourth, that when historians wished to speak directly forward, the Gatekeepers used their not having filed a prior notice or that there was no roster today as excuses.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, that when historians wished to speak directly forward, the Gatekeepers used their not having filed a prior notice or that there was no roster today as excuses.

sentences.zh: 乞自今直前言事，不必預牒閣門，及以有無班次為拘。

translations.literal: He asked that from now on historians speaking directly forward need not file prior notice with the Gatekeepers, nor be bound by whether there was a roster.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that from now on historians speaking directly forward need not file prior notice with the Gatekeepers, nor be bound by whether there was a roster.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed this.

sentences.zh: 兼侍講、國史院編修官。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Lecturer and compiler in the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently Lecturer and compiler in the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 因講《禮記》，曰：「君以禮為重，禮以分為重，分以名為重，願陛下無以名器輕假人。」

translations.literal: When lecturing on the Book of Rites he said: "The ruler takes ritual as weighty; ritual takes division as weighty; division takes names as weighty—I hope Your Majesty will not lightly lend titles and offices to others."
translations.idiomatic: When lecturing on the Book of Rites he said, "The ruler takes ritual as weighty; ritual takes division as weighty; division takes names as weighty—I hope Your Majesty will not lightly lend titles and offices to others."

sentences.zh: 又進言乞都建康，謂：「漢高入關中，光武守信都。

translations.literal: He also advanced a request to make the capital at Jiankang, saying: "Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Guanzhong; Emperor Guangwu held to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He also advanced a request to make the capital at Jiankang, saying, "Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Guanzhong; Emperor Guangwu held to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 大抵與人鬥，不搤其亢，拊其背，不能全勝。

translations.literal: In fighting a man, if you do not seize his throat and strike his back, you cannot win completely.
translations.idiomatic: In fighting a man, if you do not seize his throat and strike his back, you cannot win completely.

sentences.zh: 今日大勢，自淮以北，天下之亢與背也，建康則搤之拊之之地也。

translations.literal: Today's great momentum: north of the Huai is the throat and back of the realm; Jiankang is the place to seize and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Today's great momentum: north of the Huai is the throat and back of the realm; Jiankang is the place to seize and strike.

sentences.zh: 若進據建康，下臨中原，此高、光興王之計也。」

translations.literal: If you advance and hold Jiankang, looking down on the Central Plain, this is the plan by which Gaozu and Guangwu rose."
translations.idiomatic: If you advance and hold Jiankang, looking down on the Central Plain, this is the plan by which Gaozu and Guangwu rose."

sentences.zh: 詔議行幸，言者請紓其期，遂以張浚視師圖恢復，侍御史王十朋贊之。

translations.literal: An edict discussed the imperial progress; speakers asked to ease the date; then Zhang Jun was sent to oversee the army and plan recovery, and the attendant censor Wang Shipeng endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict discussed the imperial progress; speakers asked to ease the date; then Zhang Jun was sent to oversee the army and plan recovery, and the attendant censor Wang Shipeng endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 克復宿州，大將李顯忠私其金帛，且與邵宏淵忿爭，軍大潰。

translations.literal: They recovered Suzhou; the great general Li Xianzhong kept the gold and silks for himself and quarreled with Shao Hongyuan; the army collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Suzhou; the great general Li Xianzhong kept the gold and silks for himself and quarreled with Shao Hongyuan; the army collapsed in great rout.

sentences.zh: 十朋自劾。

translations.literal: Shipeng impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，銓上疏願毋以小衄自沮。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry; Quan submitted a memorial asking that he not be discouraged by a small setback.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was very angry; Quan submitted a memorial asking that he not be discouraged by a small setback.

sentences.zh: 銓又言：「昔周世宗為劉旻所敗，斬敗將何徽等七十人，軍威大震，果敗旻，取淮南，定三關。

translations.literal: Quan also said: "Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou was defeated by Liu Min and beheaded the defeated generals He Hui and seventy others; military prestige shook greatly; he indeed defeated Min, took Huainan, and secured the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Quan also said, "Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou was defeated by Liu Min and beheaded the defeated generals He Hui and seventy others; military prestige shook greatly; he indeed defeated Min, took Huainan, and secured the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 夫一日戮七十將，豈復有將可用？

translations.literal: To kill seventy generals in one day—would there still be generals usable?
translations.idiomatic: To kill seventy generals in one day—would there still be generals usable?

sentences.zh: 而世宗終能恢復，非庸懦者去，則勇敢者出耶！

translations.literal: Yet Shizong in the end could recover—is it not that when the timid depart, the brave come forth!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shizong in the end could recover—is it not that when the timid depart, the brave come forth!

sentences.zh: 近宿州之敗，士死于敵者滿野，而敗軍之將以所得之金賂權貴以自解，上天見變昭然，陛下非信賞必罰以應天不可。」

translations.literal: Recently at the defeat at Suzhou, soldiers who died at the enemy's hands filled the fields, yet the defeated generals used the gold they obtained to bribe the powerful to excuse themselves; Heaven's warnings are plain; Your Majesty must use sure rewards and sure punishments to respond to Heaven—it cannot be otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Recently at the defeat at Suzhou, soldiers who died at the enemy's hands filled the fields, yet the defeated generals used the gold they obtained to bribe the powerful to excuse themselves; Heaven's warnings are plain; Your Majesty must use sure rewards and sure punishments to respond to Heaven—it cannot be otherwise."

sentences.zh: 其論納諫曰：「今廷臣以箝默為賢，容悅為忠。

translations.literal: On accepting remonstrance he said: "Now court ministers take silence as worthy and flattery as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: On accepting remonstrance he said, "Now court ministers take silence as worthy and flattery as loyal.

sentences.zh: 馴至興元之幸，所謂『一言喪邦』。」

translations.literal: This led step by step to the progress to Xingyuan—what is called 'one word loses the state.'"
translations.idiomatic: This led step by step to the progress to Xingyuan—what is called 'one word loses the state.'"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「非卿不聞此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Had it not been for you I would not have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Had it not been for you I would not have heard this."

sentences.zh: 金人求成，銓曰：「金人知陛下銳意恢復，故以甘言款我，願絕口勿言『和』字。」

translations.literal: When the Jin sought peace, Quan said: "The Jin know Your Majesty is keen to recover and therefore use sweet words to court us—I hope you will close your mouth and not speak the word 'peace.'"
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin sought peace, Quan said, "The Jin know Your Majesty is keen to recover and therefore use sweet words to court us—I hope you will close your mouth and not speak the word 'peace.'"

sentences.zh: 上以邊事全倚張浚，而王之望、尹穡專主和排浚，銓廷責之。

translations.literal: The emperor relied wholly on Zhang Jun for frontier affairs, while Wang Zhiwang and Yin Ji specialized in advocating peace and opposing Jun; Quan rebuked them at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied wholly on Zhang Jun for frontier affairs, while Wang Zhiwang and Yin Ji specialized in advocating peace and opposing Jun; Quan rebuked them at court.

sentences.zh: 兼權中書舍人、同修國史。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Acting Drafting Official in the Central Secretariat and associate compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently Acting Drafting Official in the Central Secretariat and associate compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 張浚之子栻賜金紫，銓繳奏之，謂不當如此待勳臣子。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun's son Shi was granted gold and purple; Quan returned the memorial, saying one should not treat a meritorious minister's son thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun's son Shi was granted gold and purple; Quan returned the memorial, saying one should not treat a meritorious minister's son thus.

sentences.zh: 浚雅與銓厚，不顧也。

translations.literal: Jun had long been close to Quan, but Quan paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had long been close to Quan, but Quan paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔以和戎遣使，大詢于庭，侍從、台諫預議者凡十有四人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict sent envoys to make peace with the Rong; there was great inquiry in court; attendants and remonstrators who took part in the preliminary discussion numbered fourteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict sent envoys to make peace with the Rong; there was great inquiry in court; attendants and remonstrators who took part in the preliminary discussion numbered fourteen in all.

sentences.zh: 主和者半，可否者半，言不可和者銓一人而已，乃獨上一議曰：「京師失守自耿南仲主和，二聖播遷自何㮚主和，維揚失守自汪伯彥、黃潛善主和，完顏亮之變自秦檜主和。

translations.literal: Half advocated peace, half were undecided, and only Quan alone said peace was impossible; he alone submitted a memorial saying: "The capital's fall began with Geng Nanzhong's advocacy of peace; the Two Sovereigns' wanderings began with He Zhuo's advocacy of peace; Yangzhou's fall began with Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan's advocacy of peace; Wanyan Liang's revolt began with Qin Hui's advocacy of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Half advocated peace, half were undecided, and only Quan alone said peace was impossible; he alone submitted a memorial saying, "The capital's fall began with Geng Nanzhong's advocacy of peace; the Two Sovereigns' wanderings began with He Zhuo's advocacy of peace; Yangzhou's fall began with Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan's advocacy of peace; Wanyan Liang's revolt began with Qin Hui's advocacy of peace.

sentences.zh: 議者乃曰：『外雖和而內不忘戰。』

translations.literal: The debaters then say: 'Outwardly at peace yet inwardly not forgetting war.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters then say, 'Outwardly at peace yet inwardly not forgetting war.

sentences.zh: 此向來權臣誤國之言也。

translations.literal: This is the language by which powerful ministers of old misled the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the language by which powerful ministers of old misled the state.

sentences.zh: 一溺於和，不能自振，尚能戰乎？」

translations.literal: Once drowned in peace, unable to rouse oneself—can one still fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Once drowned in peace, unable to rouse oneself—can one still fight?"

sentences.zh: 除宗正少卿，乞補外，不許。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; he begged an outside post and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; he begged an outside post and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 先是，金將蒲察徒穆、大周仁以泗州降，蕭琦以軍百人降，詔並為節度使。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin generals Pucha Tumu and Da Zhouren had surrendered Sizhou, and Xiao Qi surrendered with a hundred soldiers; an edict made them all military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jin generals Pucha Tumu and Da Zhouren had surrendered Sizhou, and Xiao Qi surrendered with a hundred soldiers; an edict made them all military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 銓言：「受降古所難，六朝七得河南之地，不旋踵而皆失；

translations.literal: Quan said: "Accepting surrender has always been difficult; the Six Dynasties seven times gained the lands south of the River, and within a turning of the heel all were lost again;
translations.idiomatic: Quan said, "Accepting surrender has always been difficult; the Six Dynasties seven times gained the lands south of the River, and within a turning of the heel all were lost again;

sentences.zh: 梁武時侯景以河南來奔，未幾而陷台城；

translations.literal: under Emperor Wu of Liang, Hou Jing came from south of the River to surrender, and before long he took Taicheng;
translations.idiomatic: under Emperor Wu of Liang, Hou Jing came from south of the River to surrender, and before long he took Taicheng;

sentences.zh: 宣、政間郭藥師自燕雲來降，未幾為中國患。

translations.literal: in the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns Guo Yaoshi came from Yan and Yun to surrender, and before long he became a scourge to China.
translations.idiomatic: in the Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns Guo Yaoshi came from Yan and Yun to surrender, and before long he became a scourge to China.

sentences.zh: 今金之三大將內附，高其爵祿，優其部曲，以系中原之心，善矣。

translations.literal: Now the Jin's three great generals have come within to submit; to raise their ranks and salaries and treat their followers generously in order to bind the hearts of the Central Plain—this is good.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Jin's three great generals have come within to submit; to raise their ranks and salaries and treat their followers generously in order to bind the hearts of the Central Plain—this is good.

sentences.zh: 然處之近地，萬一包藏禍心，或為內應，後將噬臍，願勿任以兵柄，遷其眾於湖、廣以絕後患。」

translations.literal: Yet if they are placed near at hand, should they harbor evil intent or serve as inside agents, later you will bite your navel—I hope you will not give them military authority and will move their followers to Hu and Guang to cut off later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if they are placed near at hand, should they harbor evil intent or serve as inside agents, later you will bite your navel—I hope you will not give them military authority and will move their followers to Hu and Guang to cut off later trouble."

sentences.zh: 二年，兼國子祭酒，尋除權兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was concurrently Director of the Imperial University, and soon made Acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was concurrently Director of the Imperial University, and soon made Acting Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 八月，上以災異避殿減膳，詔廷臣言闕政急務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because of portents and disasters the emperor left the hall and reduced his meals; an edict asked court ministers to speak on neglected policies and urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, because of portents and disasters the emperor left the hall and reduced his meals; an edict asked court ministers to speak on neglected policies and urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 銓以振災為急務，議和為闕政，其議和之書曰：

translations.literal: Quan took relieving disaster as the urgent task and peace talks as the neglected policy; his memorial on peace reads:
translations.idiomatic: Quan took relieving disaster as the urgent task and peace talks as the neglected policy; his memorial on peace reads:

sentences.zh: 自靖康迄今凡四十年，三遭大變，皆在和議，則醜虜之不可與和，彰彰然矣。

translations.literal: From Jingkang to now forty years have passed; three great calamities were all in peace agreements—then the ugly barbarians' unfitness for peace is clear indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingkang to now forty years have passed; three great calamities were all in peace agreements—then the ugly barbarians' unfitness for peace is clear indeed.

sentences.zh: 肉食鄙夫，萬口一談，牢不可破。

translations.literal: Meat-eating vulgar fellows, ten thousand mouths with one talk, firmly unbreakable.
translations.idiomatic: Meat-eating vulgar fellows, ten thousand mouths with one talk, firmly unbreakable.

sentences.zh: 非不知和議之害，而爭言為和者，是有三說焉：曰偷懦，曰苟安，曰附會。

translations.literal: It is not that they do not know the harm of peace talks, yet those who contend to speak for peace have three arguments: called timid cowardice, called seeking a false peace, called currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that they do not know the harm of peace talks, yet those who contend to speak for peace have three arguments: called timid cowardice, called seeking a false peace, called currying favor.

sentences.zh: 偷懦則不知立國，苟安則不戒鴆毒，附會則覬得美官，小人之情狀具於此矣。

translations.literal: Timid cowardice does not know how to establish a state; false peace does not guard against poison; currying favor hopes to obtain a fine office—the petty man's disposition is fully shown here.
translations.idiomatic: Timid cowardice does not know how to establish a state; false peace does not guard against poison; currying favor hopes to obtain a fine office—the petty man's disposition is fully shown here.

sentences.zh: 今日之議若成，則有可吊者十；

translations.literal: If today's deliberation succeeds, there are ten things to mourn;
translations.idiomatic: If today's deliberation succeeds, there are ten things to mourn;

sentences.zh: 若不成，則有可賀者亦十。

translations.literal: if it does not succeed, there are also ten things to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: if it does not succeed, there are also ten things to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 請為陛下極言之。

translations.literal: I ask to set them forth fully for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to set them forth fully for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 何謂可吊者十？

translations.literal: What are the ten things to mourn?
translations.idiomatic: What are the ten things to mourn?

sentences.zh: 真宗皇帝時，宰相李沆謂王旦曰：「我死，公必為相，切勿與虜講和。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhenzong, the chief minister Li Hang said to Wang Dan: "When I die you will surely become chief minister—by all means do not make peace with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Zhenzong, the chief minister Li Hang said to Wang Dan, "When I die you will surely become chief minister—by all means do not make peace with the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 吾聞出則無敵國外患，如是者國常亡，若與虜和，自此中國必多事矣。」

translations.literal: I have heard: when abroad there are no enemy states and no external troubles, states often perish; if you make peace with the barbarians, from this China will surely have many troubles."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when abroad there are no enemy states and no external troubles, states often perish; if you make peace with the barbarians, from this China will surely have many troubles."

sentences.zh: 旦殊不以為然。

translations.literal: Dan by no means thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Dan by no means thought it so.

sentences.zh: 既而遂和，海內乾耗，旦始悔不用文靖之言。

translations.literal: Before long peace was made; within the seas resources were drained dry; Dan only then regretted not using Wenkang's words.
translations.idiomatic: Before long peace was made; within the seas resources were drained dry; Dan only then regretted not using Wenkang's words.

sentences.zh: 此可吊者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 中原謳吟思歸之人，日夜引領望陛下拯溺救焚，不啻赤子之望慈父母，一與虜和，則中原絕望，後悔何及。

translations.literal: People in the Central Plain who sing and long to return, day and night stretch their necks hoping Your Majesty will save the drowning and rescue the burning—not less than an infant looking to a loving parent; once peace is made with the barbarians, the Central Plain's hope is cut off—what regret can compare?
translations.idiomatic: People in the Central Plain who sing and long to return, day and night stretch their necks hoping Your Majesty will save the drowning and rescue the burning—not less than an infant looking to a loving parent; once peace is made with the barbarians, the Central Plain's hope is cut off—what regret can compare?

sentences.zh: 此可吊者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 海、泗今日之藩籬咽喉也，彼得海、泗，且決吾藩籬以瞰吾室，扼吾咽喉以制吾命，則兩淮決不可保。

translations.literal: Hai and Si are today's barrier and throat; if they obtain Hai and Si, they will tear our barrier to overlook our hall and seize our throat to control our fate—then the two Huai cannot possibly be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Hai and Si are today's barrier and throat; if they obtain Hai and Si, they will tear our barrier to overlook our hall and seize our throat to control our fate—then the two Huai cannot possibly be kept.

sentences.zh: 兩淮不保，則大江決不可守，大江不守，則江、浙決不可安。

translations.literal: If the two Huai cannot be kept, the Great River cannot possibly be held; if the Great River is not held, Jiang and Zhe cannot possibly be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If the two Huai cannot be kept, the Great River cannot possibly be held; if the Great River is not held, Jiang and Zhe cannot possibly be secure.

sentences.zh: 此可吊者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 紹興戊午，和議即成，檜建議遣二三大臣如路允迪等，分往南京等州交割歸地。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year of Shaoxing, when the peace agreement was made, Hui proposed sending two or three great ministers such as Lu Yundi to Nanjing and other prefectures in turn to hand over returned territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year of Shaoxing, when the peace agreement was made, Hui proposed sending two or three great ministers such as Lu Yundi to Nanjing and other prefectures in turn to hand over returned territory.

sentences.zh: 一旦叛盟，劫執允迪等，遂下親征之詔，虜復請和。

translations.literal: In a day they broke the covenant, seized and held Yundi and the rest, and then issued an edict for a personal campaign; the barbarians again asked for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In a day they broke the covenant, seized and held Yundi and the rest, and then issued an edict for a personal campaign; the barbarians again asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 其反覆變詐如此，檜猶不悟，奉之如初，事之愈謹，賂之愈厚，卒有逆亮之變，驚動輦轂。

translations.literal: Their reversals and deceits were thus; Hui still did not awaken, served them as at first, attended them ever more carefully, bribed them ever more heavily—at last came Wanyan Liang's revolt, shaking the imperial carriage precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Their reversals and deceits were thus; Hui still did not awaken, served them as at first, attended them ever more carefully, bribed them ever more heavily—at last came Wanyan Liang's revolt, shaking the imperial carriage precinct.

sentences.zh: 太上謀欲入海，行朝居民一空，覆轍不遠，忽而不戒，臣恐後車又將覆也。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor planned to go to sea; the traveling court's residents were emptied in a day; the overturned cart is not far off—if you neglect and do not guard, your servant fears the rear cart will overturn again.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor planned to go to sea; the traveling court's residents were emptied in a day; the overturned cart is not far off—if you neglect and do not guard, your servant fears the rear cart will overturn again.

sentences.zh: 此可吊者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 紹興之和，首議決不與歸正人，口血未乾，盡變前議。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing peace, the first agreement firmly decided not to hand over those who had returned to the orthodox side; the blood on the lips was not yet dry when all prior agreements were changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaoxing peace, the first agreement firmly decided not to hand over those who had returned to the orthodox side; the blood on the lips was not yet dry when all prior agreements were changed.

sentences.zh: 凡歸正之人一切遣還，如程師回、趙良嗣等聚族數百，幾為蕭牆憂。

translations.literal: All who had returned to the orthodox side were sent back in one sweep; such as Cheng Shihui and Zhao Liangsi and others, clans numbering hundreds, nearly became trouble within the curtained wall.
translations.idiomatic: All who had returned to the orthodox side were sent back in one sweep; such as Cheng Shihui and Zhao Liangsi and others, clans numbering hundreds, nearly became trouble within the curtained wall.

sentences.zh: 今必盡索歸正之人，與之則反側生變，不與則虜決不肯但已。

translations.literal: Now they must demand all who returned to the orthodox side; if you hand them over, those who waver will breed change; if you do not, the barbarians will certainly not simply stop.
translations.idiomatic: Now they must demand all who returned to the orthodox side; if you hand them over, those who waver will breed change; if you do not, the barbarians will certainly not simply stop.

sentences.zh: 夫反側則肘腋之變深，虜決不肯但已，則必別起釁端，猝有逆亮之謀，不知何以待之。

translations.literal: If those who waver breed change, trouble at the elbow and armpit grows deep; if the barbarians will not simply stop, they must raise some other quarrel—suddenly there is a plot like Wanyan Liang's, and one does not know how to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: If those who waver breed change, trouble at the elbow and armpit grows deep; if the barbarians will not simply stop, they must raise some other quarrel—suddenly there is a plot like Wanyan Liang's, and one does not know how to meet it.

sentences.zh: 此可吊者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 自檜當國二十年間，竭民膏血以餌犬羊，迄今府庫無旬月之儲，千村萬落生理蕭然，重以蝗蟲水潦。

translations.literal: In the twenty years while Hui held the state, he drained the people's fat and blood to feed dogs and sheep; to this day the treasuries have not a ten-day store; a thousand villages and ten thousand hamlets see livelihood wither, compounded by locusts and floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty years while Hui held the state, he drained the people's fat and blood to feed dogs and sheep; to this day the treasuries have not a ten-day store; a thousand villages and ten thousand hamlets see livelihood wither, compounded by locusts and floods.

sentences.zh: 自此復和，則蠹國害民，殆有甚焉者矣。

translations.literal: From this if peace is made again, the harm to state and people will have something even worse.
translations.idiomatic: From this if peace is made again, the harm to state and people will have something even worse.

sentences.zh: 此可吊者六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth thing to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 今日之患，兵費已廣，養兵之外又增歲幣，且少以十年計之，其費無慮數千億。

translations.literal: Today's trouble: military costs are already vast; beyond maintaining troops there is added yearly tribute—and counting a mere ten years, the expense cannot be less than several hundred billion.
translations.idiomatic: Today's trouble: military costs are already vast; beyond maintaining troops there is added yearly tribute—and counting a mere ten years, the expense cannot be less than several hundred billion.

sentences.zh: 而歲幣之外，又有私覿之費；

translations.literal: And beyond the yearly tribute coins, there are again expenses for private audiences;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond yearly tribute, there are also the costs of private audiences;

sentences.zh: 私覿之外，又有賀正、生辰之使；

translations.literal: Beyond private audiences, there are again envoys for New Year's congratulations and birthday celebrations;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond private audiences come envoys to congratulate the New Year and celebrate birthdays;

sentences.zh: 賀正、生辰之外，又有泛使。

translations.literal: Beyond New Year's and birthday missions, there are again general envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond those come yet more ad hoc embassies.

sentences.zh: 一使未去，一使復來，生民疲於奔命，帑廩涸於將迎，瘠中國以肥虜，陛下何憚而為之。

translations.literal: One envoy has not left, another envoy comes again; the living people weary at running on orders; the storehouses drain in receiving and seeing off; lean China to fatten the barbarians—why does Your Majesty shrink from acting?
translations.idiomatic: One envoy has barely left when another arrives; the people exhaust themselves running to and fro; the treasury runs dry on receptions and send-offs; China is bled thin to enrich the enemy—why does Your Majesty shrink from stopping this?

sentences.zh: 此其可吊者七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh matter for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 側聞虜人嫚書，欲書御名，欲去國號「大」字，欲用再拜。

translations.literal: I have heard on the side that the barbarians' contemptuous letter wishes to write the Emperor's personal name, wishes to remove the character "Great" from the state name, wishes to use the double bow.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in their insulting correspondence the Jin wish to inscribe Your Majesty's personal name, strike the character "Great" from our state title, and require the double bow.

sentences.zh: 議者以為繁文小節不必計較，臣切以為議者可斬也。

translations.literal: Those who discuss say these are elaborate trifles not needing comparison; your servant urgently thinks those who discuss deserve beheading.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue these are trivial formalities not worth quibbling over—I maintain that those who argue thus deserve the headsman's axe.

sentences.zh: 夫四郊多壘，卿大夫之辱；

translations.literal: When the four suburbs have many ramparts, it is the shame of ministers and grandees;
translations.idiomatic: Ramparts crowding the four suburbs—that is the shame of the court.

sentences.zh: 楚子問鼎，義士之所深恥；

translations.literal: The lord of Chu asking about the tripods—what righteous men deeply abhor;
translations.idiomatic: When the lord of Chu asked about the cauldrons—righteous men were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 「獻納」二字，富弼以死爭之。

translations.literal: The two characters "present and receive"—Fu Bi contended with his life for them.
translations.idiomatic: Over the two words "present and receive," Fu Bi fought as if his life depended on it.

sentences.zh: 今醜虜橫行與多壘孰辱？

translations.literal: Now the vile barbarians run rampant, and many ramparts—which shame is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Which is the greater disgrace—the enemy rampant, or ramparts crowding the suburbs?

sentences.zh: 國號大小與鼎輕重孰多？

translations.literal: The great or small of the state name and the light or heavy of the tripods—which is more?
translations.idiomatic: Which weighs more—the size of our state title or the weight of the royal cauldrons?

sentences.zh: 「獻納」二字與再拜孰重？

translations.literal: The two characters "present and receive" and the double bow—which is heavier?
translations.idiomatic: Which carries more weight—the words "present and receive," or the double bow?

sentences.zh: 臣子欲君父屈己以從之，則是多壘不足辱，問鼎不必恥，「獻納」不必爭。
