translations.literal: If ministers wish the lord and father to bend himself to follow them, then many ramparts are not shame enough, asking about tripods need not be abhorred, "present and receive" need not be contended.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers would have the Emperor and father humiliate himself to comply, then ramparts at the gates are no disgrace, inquiring after the cauldrons no cause for shame, and "present and receive" not worth fighting over.

sentences.zh: 此其可吊者八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth matter for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 臣恐再拜不已必至稱臣，稱臣不已必至請降，請降不已必至納土，納土不已必至銜壁，銜壁不已必至輿櫬，輿櫬不已必至如晉帝青衣行酒然後為快。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that if the double bow does not stop, it must reach calling oneself subject; if calling subject does not stop, it must reach begging to surrender; if begging surrender does not stop, it must reach offering up territory; if offering territory does not stop, it must reach bearing jade in the mouth; if bearing jade does not stop, it must reach carrying the coffin; if carrying the coffin does not stop, it must reach the point where, like the Jin emperor in blue robes serving wine, only then are they satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once the double bow begins, it will lead inevitably to calling ourselves subjects; subjects to begging surrender; surrender to yielding territory; yielding territory to the jade-in-mouth ritual; that to the coffin-on-a-cart procession—and only when we are reduced, like the Jin emperor serving wine in blue robes, will they be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 此其可吊者九也。

translations.literal: This is the ninth matter for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 事至於此，求為匹夫尚可得乎？

translations.literal: When matters reach this, to seek to be a common man—is it still obtainable?
translations.idiomatic: When things come to this pass, can one even hope to live as an ordinary subject?

sentences.zh: 此其可吊者十也。

translations.literal: This is the tenth matter for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth thing to mourn.

sentences.zh: 竊觀今日之勢，和決不成，儻乾剛獨斷，追回使者魏杞、康湑等，絕請和之議以鼓戰士，下哀痛之詔以收民心，天下庶乎其可為矣。

translations.literal: I privately observe today's situation—peace will certainly not succeed; if Your Majesty alone resolutely decides, recalls envoys Wei Qi, Kang Xu and others, cuts off peace-seeking discussion to rouse warriors, issues a grief-stricken edict to gather the people's hearts, perhaps under Heaven something can be done.
translations.idiomatic: From what I can see, peace is out of the question; but if Your Majesty acted with resolute authority—recalling envoys Wei Qi, Kang Xu, and the rest, cutting off all talk of peace to rouse the soldiers, and issuing a heartfelt edict of grief to rally the people—perhaps something could still be salvaged for the realm.

sentences.zh: 如此則有可賀者亦十：省數千億之歲幣，一也；

translations.literal: If so, there would also be ten things to celebrate: saving several hundred billion in yearly tribute—first;
translations.idiomatic: If so, there would be ten things to celebrate: saving hundreds of billions in yearly tribute—first;

sentences.zh: 專意武備，足食足兵，二也；

translations.literal: Devoting effort to military readiness, ample food and ample troops—second;
translations.idiomatic: Devoting attention to military readiness, with ample food and ample troops—second;

sentences.zh: 無書名之恥，三也；

translations.literal: No shame of writing the personal name—third;
translations.idiomatic: No humiliation of inscribing the personal name—third;

sentences.zh: 無去「大」之辱，四也；

translations.literal: No humiliation of removing "Great"—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: No insult of stripping the character "Great"—fourth;

sentences.zh: 無再拜之屈，五也；

translations.literal: No abasement of the double bow—fifth;
translations.idiomatic: No debasement of the double bow—fifth;

sentences.zh: 無稱臣之忿，六也；

translations.literal: No rage-inducing subject-status—sixth;
translations.idiomatic: No indignity of calling ourselves subjects—sixth;

sentences.zh: 無請降之禍，七也；

translations.literal: No calamity of begging surrender—seventh;
translations.idiomatic: No disaster of begging to surrender—seventh;

sentences.zh: 無納土之悲，八也；

translations.literal: No grief of yielding territory—eighth;
translations.idiomatic: No sorrow of yielding territory—eighth;

sentences.zh: 無銜璧、輿櫬之酷，九也；

translations.literal: No brutality of jade-in-mouth and coffin-bearing—ninth;
translations.idiomatic: No horror of the jade-in-mouth and coffin-on-a-cart rituals—ninth;

sentences.zh: 無青衣行酒之冤，十也。

translations.literal: No injustice of blue-robed wine-serving—tenth.
translations.idiomatic: No outrage of the blue-robed wine-serving humiliation—tenth.

sentences.zh: 去十吊而就十賀，利害較然，雖三尺童稚亦知之，而陛下不悟。

translations.literal: Leaving ten mournings and taking ten celebrations—the harm and benefit are clearly weighed; even a three-foot child knows it, yet Your Majesty does not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off ten grounds for mourning and gain ten grounds for celebration—the balance of harm and benefit is obvious; even a child knows it, yet Your Majesty does not see it.

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏》謂無勇者為婦人，今日舉朝之士皆婦人也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says that one without courage is a woman—in today's court, all are women.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says that the cowardly are women—in today's court, every man is a woman.

sentences.zh: 如以臣言為不然，乞賜流放竄殛，以為臣子出位犯分之戒。

translations.literal: If my words are held wrong, I beg to be granted exile, banishment, or execution, as a warning to ministers who overstep rank and violate propriety.
translations.idiomatic: If you deem my words wrong, I beg exile, banishment, or death—as a warning to ministers who overstep their station.

sentences.zh: 自符離之敗，朝論急於和戎，棄唐、鄧、海、泗四州與虜矣。

translations.literal: Since the defeat at Fuli, court opinion was urgent for peace with the barbarians, abandoning the four prefectures Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Fuli, the court rushed toward peace with the Jin and ceded the four prefectures of Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si.

sentences.zh: 金又欲得商、秦地，邀歲幣，留使者魏杞，分兵攻淮。

translations.literal: Jin again wanted Shang and Qin territory, pressed for yearly tribute, detained envoy Wei Qi, and divided troops to attack the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin also demanded the Shang and Qin regions, pressed for yearly tribute, detained envoy Wei Qi, and divided forces to attack the Huai.

sentences.zh: 以本職措置浙西、淮東海道。

translations.literal: With his original post he arranged matters on the Zhexi and Huaidong sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: In his original capacity he managed affairs on the Zhexi and Huaidong sea routes.

sentences.zh: 時金使僕散忠義、紇石烈志寧之兵號八十萬，劉寶棄楚州，王彥棄昭關，濠、滁皆陷。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin dispatched Pusan Zhongyi and Heshilie Zhining's armies claiming eight hundred thousand; Liu Bao abandoned Chuzhou, Wang Yan abandoned Zhaoguan; Hao and Chu both fell.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jin sent the armies of Pusan Zhongyi and Heshilie Zhining, said to number eight hundred thousand; Liu Bao abandoned Chuzhou, Wang Yan abandoned Zhaoguan; Hao and Chu both fell.

sentences.zh: 惟高郵守臣陳敏拒敵射陽湖，而大將李寶預求密詔為自安計，擁兵不救。

translations.literal: Only Gaoyou's defending official Chen Min resisted the enemy at Sheyang Lake, while Grand General Li Bao had beforehand sought a secret edict as a plan for his own safety and held his troops without rescuing.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chen Min, the defending official of Gaoyou, held the enemy at Sheyang Lake, while Grand General Li Bao had already obtained a secret edict to protect himself and kept his troops back without aiding.

sentences.zh: 銓劾奏之，曰：「臣受詔令范榮備淮，李寶備江，緩急相援。

translations.literal: Quan impeached and memorialized, saying: "Your servant received an edict ordering Fan Rong to guard the Huai and Li Bao to guard the Jiang, aiding each other in urgent or slack times.
translations.idiomatic: Quan impeached him and memorialized: "Your servant received orders that Fan Rong should defend the Huai and Li Bao the Yangzi, supporting each other as need arose.

sentences.zh: 今寶視敏弗救，若射陽失守，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: Now Bao sees Min and does not rescue—if Sheyang is lost, the great matter is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Now Bao watches Min go unsupported—if Sheyang falls, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 寶懼，始出師掎角。

translations.literal: Bao feared, and only then marched out in pincer support.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao, alarmed, finally marched out in coordinated support.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，河冰皆合，銓先持鐵錘錘冰，士皆用命，金人遂退。

translations.literal: At the time heavy snow fell and river ice all joined; Quan first took an iron hammer to break ice, and soldiers all obeyed with devotion; the Jin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow had fallen and the rivers were frozen solid; Quan took up an iron hammer and broke the ice first, and the men all fought with spirit—the Jin then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 久之，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was made commissioner of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed commissioner of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，以集英殿修撰知漳州，改泉州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao, as Compiler of the Hall for Advancing Worthies he governed Zhangzhou, then was transferred to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiandao era he served as prefect of Zhangzhou as Compiler of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, then was transferred to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 趣奏事，留為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to report on affairs, he was retained as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Urgently summoned to report on state affairs, he was kept on as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「少康以一旅復禹績，今陛下富有四海，非特一旅，而即位九年，復禹之效尚未赫然。」

translations.literal: Entering audience he said: "Shaokang with one brigade restored Yu's achievement; now Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas—not merely one brigade—yet nine years on the throne, the effect of restoring Yu is not yet conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said: "Shaokang restored Yu's legacy with a single brigade; Your Majesty holds all within the four seas—not merely one brigade—yet nine years on the throne, and the recovery is still nowhere in sight.

sentences.zh: 又言：「四方多水旱，左右不以告，謀國者之過也，宜令有司速為先備。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The four quarters have much flood and drought; those at your side do not report it—the fault of those who plan for the state; Your Majesty should order the responsible offices to prepare beforehand with speed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Floods and droughts afflict the realm, yet those around you do not report them—a failure of those who govern; the responsible offices should be ordered to prepare at once.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕。

translations.literal: He requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 七年，除寶文閣待制，留經筵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Attendant Draftsman of the Baowen Pavilion and retained at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Attendant Draftsman of the Baowen Pavilion and kept at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 求去，以敷文閣直學士與外祠。

translations.literal: Seeking to leave, he was given the title of Direct Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and an outside directorship.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked to leave, he was given the title Direct Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion with an outside temple directorship.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，猶以歸陵寢、復故疆為言，上曰：「朕志也。」

translations.literal: At farewell audience he still spoke of returning to the imperial tombs and recovering the old territory; the Emperor said: "That is my aim too.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he again spoke of restoring the imperial tombs and recovering lost territory; the Emperor said: "That is my aim as well.

sentences.zh: 且問今何歸，銓曰：「歸廬陵，臣向在嶺海嘗訓傳諸經，欲成此書。」

translations.literal: And asked where he would now return, Quan said: "I return to Luling; your servant, while in the Lingnan seas, once lectured on and transmitted the various classics and wishes to complete this book.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where he would go, Quan replied: "To Luling—I once lectured on the classics in the Lingnan region and wish to finish that work.

sentences.zh: 特賜通天犀帶以寵之。

translations.literal: He was specially granted a tongtian rhinoceros-horn belt to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted a tongtian rhinoceros-horn belt as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 銓歸，上所著《易》、《春秋》、《周禮》、《禮記解》，詔藏秘書省。

translations.literal: Quan returned and submitted his commentaries on the Changes, Spring and Autumn, Rites of Zhou, and Record of Rites; an edict ordered them stored in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Quan returned and submitted his commentaries on the Changes, Spring and Autumn, Rites of Zhou, and Record of Rites; an edict ordered them deposited in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋復元官，升龍圖閣學士、提舉太平興國宮，轉提舉玉隆萬壽宮，進端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Soon his original rank was restored; he was promoted to Academician of the Longtu Pavilion and commissioner of Taiping Xingguo Palace, transferred to commissioner of Yulong Wanshou Palace, and advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his original rank was restored; he rose to Academician of the Longtu Pavilion and commissioner of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, then commissioner of the Yulong Wanshou Palace, and was advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 六年，召歸經筵，銓引疾力辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned back to the Classics Colloquium; Quan cited illness and forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled to the Classics Colloquium; Quan pleaded illness and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 七年，以資政殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he retired as Academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired with the rank of Academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 有《澹庵集》一百卷行於世。

translations.literal: His Collection from the Tranquil Hermitage in one hundred volumes circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collection from the Tranquil Hermitage, one hundred volumes, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 孫槻、榘，皆至尚書。

translations.literal: His grandsons Gui and Ju both reached the Ministry Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Gui and Ju both rose to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，盜起旁郡，官吏悉逃去，順昌民以剛為命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, bandits rose in neighboring prefectures; officials all fled; the people of Shunchang took Gang as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 1, bandits rose in neighboring prefectures and officials fled; the people of Shunchang looked to Gang as their leader.

sentences.zh: 剛諭從盜者使反業，既而他盜入順昌，部使者檄剛撫定。

translations.literal: Gang admonished those who followed bandits to return to their occupations; afterward other bandits entered Shunchang; the circuit envoy ordered Gang to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Gang persuaded those who had joined the bandits to return to their livelihoods; when other bandits entered Shunchang, the circuit envoy ordered Gang to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 剛遣長子遲諭賊，賊知剛父子有信義，亦散去。

translations.literal: Gang sent his eldest son Chi to admonish the bandits; the bandits knew the Gang father and son had integrity and also dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Gang sent his eldest son Chi to reason with the bandits; knowing the Gangs for men of integrity, they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 除本路提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was appointed Circuit Intendant of Prisons for his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed circuit intendant of prisons for his route.

sentences.zh: 尋召為吏部員外郎，言：「古者天子必有親兵自將，所以備不虞而強主威，漢北軍、唐神策之類也。

translations.literal: Soon summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; he said: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven necessarily had personal troops he himself commanded, to guard against the unexpected and strengthen sovereign authority—the Han Northern Army, Tang Shence Corps, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he said: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven always kept personal troops under his own command—to guard against the unexpected and strengthen imperial authority—as with the Han Northern Army and the Tang Shence Corps.

sentences.zh: 祖宗軍制尤嚴。

translations.literal: Our ancestors' military system was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: The military system of our founders was especially strict.

sentences.zh: 願稽舊制，選精銳為親兵，居則以為衛，動則以為中軍，此強幹弱枝之道。」

translations.literal: I wish to examine the old system, select the elite as personal troops—at rest using them as guard, in motion using them as central army—this is the way of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we review the old system, select the elite for personal troops—guard at rest, central army in the field—strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.

sentences.zh: 又言：「國家艱難已極，今方圖新，若會稽誠非久駐之地。

translations.literal: He also said: "The state's hardship has reached the extreme; now we are planning renewal; Kuaiji is truly not a place to stay long.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The state's hardship has reached its limit; as we plan renewal, Kuaiji is no place to linger.

sentences.zh: 請經營建康，親擁六師往為固守計，以杜金人窺伺之意。」

translations.literal: I ask to develop Jiankang, personally leading the Six Armies there as a plan for firm defense, to cut off the Jin people's intent to watch and wait.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we develop Jiankang and that Your Majesty personally lead the Six Armies there to hold firm, cutting off the Jin's designs.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人、權吏部侍郎兼侍講，除給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist, Acting Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Court Lecturer, and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Diarist, Acting Vice Minister of Personnel and Court Lecturer, then appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，復拜給事中。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he mourned; when mourning ended he was again appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he was again appointed Censor-in-Chief when the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 剛言：「國不可一日無兵，兵不可一日無食。

translations.literal: Gang said: "The state cannot go a day without troops; troops cannot go a day without food.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said: "The state cannot go a day without armies, nor armies a day without provisions.

sentences.zh: 今諸將之兵備江、淮，不知幾萬，初無儲蓄，日待哺于東南之轉餉，浙民已困，欲救此患莫若屯田。」

translations.literal: Now the generals' troops guarding Jiang and Huai—I know not how many tens of thousands—at first had no stores, daily awaiting feeding from southeast transport of supplies; the people of Zhe are already exhausted; to remedy this ill nothing is better than garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: The generals' troops on the Jiang and Huai number tens of thousands yet have no reserves, living day to day on grain shipped from the southeast; the people of Zhe are already exhausted—nothing would remedy this better than garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 因獻三說，將校有能射耕，當加優賞，每耕田一頃，與轉一資；

translations.literal: He therefore submitted three proposals: commanders and officers able to shoot and farm should receive extra rewards; for each hectare of farmland tilled, grant one promotion in rank;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three proposals: officers who could fight and farm should receive special rewards, with one rank promotion for each hectare tilled;

sentences.zh: 百姓願耕，假以糧種，復以租賦。

translations.literal: Common people willing to farm, lend them grain and seed, and reduce their rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: for commoners willing to farm, lend grain and seed and reduce rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 上令都督府措置。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Grand Commandery to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the Grand Commandery to implement the plan.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷推究章惇、蔡卞誤國之罪，追貶其身，仍詔子孫毋得官中朝。

translations.literal: At the time the court investigated the crimes of Zhang Dun and Cai Bian in harming the state, posthumously demoted them, and further edicted that their descendants should not hold office in the central court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court investigated Zhang Dun and Cai Bian for their crimes against the state, posthumously demoted them, and decreed that their descendants could not hold office at court.

sentences.zh: 至是章傑自崇道觀知婺州，章僅自太府丞提舉江東茶鹽事。

translations.literal: At this point Zhang Jie from Chongdao Abbey became prefect of Wuzhou; Zhang Jin from Grand Treasury Assistant became intendant of Jiangdong tea and salt.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Jie had gone from Chongdao Abbey to serve as prefect of Wuzhou, and Zhang Jin from Grand Treasury Assistant to intendant of Jiangdong tea and salt.

sentences.zh: 剛封還詔書，謂即如此，何以示懲，乃並與祠。

translations.literal: Gang returned the edict sealed, saying if it is just like this, how can punishment be shown—and had both given outside directorships instead.
translations.idiomatic: Gang returned the edict unopened, saying that if this was how punishment was applied, what lesson would it teach—and had both men given outside temple posts instead.

sentences.zh: 權戶部侍郎，尋遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Revenue; soon transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, then was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 求補外，除徽猷閣直學士、知漳州。

translations.literal: Seeking an outside appointment, he was made Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion and prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a provincial post, he was made Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion and prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，日有食之，詔內外官言事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year there was a solar eclipse; an edict ordered officials inside and outside to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year there was a solar eclipse, and an edict invited memorials from officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 剛言：「陛下有建國之封，所以承天意、示大公於天下後世者也，然而未遂正名者，豈非有所待耶？

translations.literal: Gang said: "Your Majesty has the fief of founding the state, by which to receive Heaven's intent and show great fairness to all under Heaven and posterity—yet the proper title has not been settled; is it not that you are waiting for something?
translations.idiomatic: Gang said: "Your Majesty holds the title of Founding Lord, meant to answer Heaven's will and show fairness to the realm and posterity—yet the heir apparent has not been formally designated; are you waiting for something?

sentences.zh: 有所待，則是應天之誠未至也。

translations.literal: If there is something waited for, then sincerity in responding to Heaven has not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: If you are waiting, then your sincerity in answering Heaven is not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 願陛下昭告藝祖在天之靈，正建國儲君之號，佈告中外，不匿厥旨。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would clearly announce to Founder Taizu's spirit in Heaven, correct the title of the heir who would found the state, proclaim it inside and outside, not hiding its intent.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty announce to the spirit of Founder Taizu in Heaven, establish the heir's title properly, and proclaim it throughout the realm without concealment.

sentences.zh: 異時雖百斯男，不復更易，天下孰敢不服。」

translations.literal: In future, though there be a hundred sons, they would not again be changed—who under Heaven would dare not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Then even should you have a hundred sons in future, the succession would never again be in doubt—who under Heaven would not submit?

sentences.zh: 上讀之聳然，即召剛趣至闕，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: The Emperor reading it was startled upright and immediately summoned Gang urgently to the palace gate, appointing him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, reading it, sat up sharply and immediately summoned Gang to court, appointing him Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 剛言：「臣職糾奸邪，當務大體，若捃摭細故，則非臣本心。」

translations.literal: Gang said: "My duty is to correct villainy and wickedness; I should attend to the larger pattern—if I pick up petty matters, that is not my true intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said: "My duty is to root out corruption; I must address the larger issues—trifling over petty offenses is not my intent.

sentences.zh: 又奏經費不支，盜賊不息，事功不立，命令不孚，及兵驕官冗之弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that revenues could not sustain expenses, bandits did not cease, achievements were not established, commands were not trusted, and the abuses of arrogant troops and redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on strained finances, persistent banditry, failure to achieve results, loss of confidence in orders, and the abuses of arrogant soldiers and bloated bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 時徽宗已崩，上遇朔望猶率群臣遙拜淵聖，剛言：「禮有隆殺，兄為君則君之，己為君則兄之可也。

translations.literal: At the time Huizong had died; on new and full moons the Emperor still led the ministers in bowing from afar to the "Profound Sage"; Gang said: "Rites have gradations of honor; when the elder brother is sovereign, treat him as sovereign; when oneself is sovereign, treating him as elder brother is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong had already died, yet on the first and fifteenth of each month the Emperor still led the court in bowing from afar to the Deposed Emperor; Gang said: "Rites have their gradations—when the elder brother was sovereign, he was treated as sovereign; now that you are sovereign, treating him as elder brother suffices.

sentences.zh: 望勉抑聖心，但歲時行家人禮于內庭。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will strive to restrain the imperial heart and only at seasonal times perform family rites within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty restrain your feelings and observe only the family rites of the seasons within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 殿前司強刺民為兵，及大將恃功希恩，所請多廢法。

translations.literal: The Palace Front Command forcibly impressed commoners as soldiers, and great generals relied on merit hoping for favor—their requests often violated law.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Front Command forcibly conscripted civilians, and great generals traded on their merit for favors, their requests often overriding the law.

sentences.zh: 剛知無不言，論列至於四五，驕橫者肅然。

translations.literal: Gang spoke without concealment, arguing the cases to four or five times; the arrogant were suddenly subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Gang held nothing back, pressing his cases repeatedly until the arrogant were brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 鄭億年與秦檜有連而得美官，剛顯疏其惡，檜銜之。

translations.literal: Zheng Yinian was connected with Qin Hui and obtained a fine office; Gang openly memorialized his evil; Hui nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yinian, connected to Qin Hui, had obtained a fine post; Gang openly memorialized against his misconduct, and Hui bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 金人叛盟，剛乞起舊相之有德望者，處以近藩，檜聞之曰：「是欲置我何地耶？」

translations.literal: When the Jin violated the treaty, Gang begged to raise an old chief councillor of virtue and renown and place him in a nearby fief; Hui hearing it said: "This intends to put me in what place?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty, Gang asked that a former chief councillor of standing be recalled and placed in a nearby fief; Hui, hearing this, said: "And where does he intend to put me?

sentences.zh: 改工部尚書，而以王次翁為中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Works, and Wang Ciweng was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was transferred to Minister of Works, and Wang Ciweng was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，邊報至，從官會都堂，剛謂億年曰：「公以百口保金人，今已背約，有何面目尚在朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: At first when border reports arrived, attendant officials met at the Secretariat Hall; Gang said to Yinian: "You guaranteed the Jin with a hundred mouths—now they have broken the treaty; with what face do you remain at court?
translations.idiomatic: When the first border reports arrived, attendant officials met at the Secretariat; Gang said to Yinian: "You pledged your family's lives that the Jin would keep the treaty—they have broken it; with what face do you remain at court?

sentences.zh: 億年奉祠去。

translations.literal: Yinian took an outside directorship and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yinian took a temple directorship and departed.

sentences.zh: 次翁與右諫議何鑄劾剛薦劉昉、陳淵，相為朋比，以徽猷閣直學士提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: Ciweng and Right Remonstrance Officer He Zhu impeached Gang for recommending Liu Fang and Chen Yuan as a faction; he was given the title Direct Academician of Huayou Pavilion and commissioner of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ciweng and Right Remonstrance Officer He Zhu impeached Gang for recommending Liu Fang and Chen Yuan as partisans; he was demoted to Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion and commissioner of the Mingdao Palace at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired.

sentences.zh: 以紹興十三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing year 13.

sentences.zh: 子四人：遲、過、遂、遽，仕皆秉麾節，邦人號為「萬石廖氏」。

translations.literal: He had four sons—Chi, Guo, Sui, and Ju—all of whom in office held military banners and seals; the people of the district called them the "Ten-Thousand-Per-Load Liao clan."
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons—Chi, Guo, Sui, and Ju—each of whom held military command; locals called them the "Wanshi Liao clan."

sentences.zh: 李迨，東平人也。

translations.literal: Li Dai was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai was a native of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖參，仕至尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Can served to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Can rose to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 迨未冠入太學，因居開封。

translations.literal: Before Dai came of age he entered the Imperial Academy and therefore lived in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age Dai entered the Imperial Academy and took up residence in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補官，初調渤海縣尉。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he entered office; his first assignment was county captain of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered office and was first posted as captain of Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 時州縣團結民兵，民起田畝中，不閑坐作進退之節，或嘩不受令，迨立賞罰以整齊之，累月皆精練，部伍如法。

translations.literal: At the time prefectures and counties were organizing militia; the men came straight from the fields, unskilled in the drill of sitting, standing, advancing, and retreating, and some clamored and refused orders. Dai established rewards and punishments to drill them; after months all were well trained, and companies and ranks conformed to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties were then organizing militia drawn from the fields—men untrained in drill, some shouting and refusing orders. Dai imposed rewards and punishments to whip them into shape; within months they were sharp and their formations followed regulation.

sentences.zh: 部刺史按閱，無一人亂行伍者，遂薦之朝，改合入官。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant inspected them; not one man broke ranks. He therefore recommended Dai to court, and Dai was changed to a regular appointee.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit intendant inspected the troops, not one man broke formation. He recommended Dai to court, and Dai was made a regular appointee.

sentences.zh: 累遷通判濟州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Vice Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 時高宗以大元帥過濟，郡守自以才不及，遜迨行州事，迨應辦軍須無闕。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong passed through Ji as Grand Marshal; the prefect, judging his own talent insufficient, yielded to Dai in administering prefectural affairs, and Dai supplied military needs without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong passed through Ji as Grand Marshal, the prefect—judging himself unequal to the task—stepped aside and let Dai run the prefecture; Dai met every military requirement without fail.

sentences.zh: 會大元帥府勸進，乘輿儀物皆未備，迨諳熟典故，裁定其制，不日而辦。

translations.literal: When the Grand Marshal's headquarters moved to establish the emperor, the regalia of the imperial carriage were not yet ready; Dai, well versed in precedent, fixed their forms, and in a few days all was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: As the Grand Marshal's staff pressed for enthronement, the imperial carriage regalia were not yet ready. Dai, steeped in precedent, settled the forms, and within days everything was in place.

sentences.zh: 上深歎賞，即除隨軍輦運。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed deeply in admiration and immediately appointed him Transport Commissioner Attached to the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply impressed, the Emperor immediately named him Transport Commissioner Attached to the Army.

sentences.zh: 上即位于南京，授山東輦運，改金部郎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne at Nanjing, Dai was granted Shandong Transport Commissioner and then transferred to Secretary of the Bureau of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor took the throne at Nanjing, Dai was made Shandong Transport Commissioner and then transferred to Secretary of the Bureau of Finance.

sentences.zh: 從駕至維揚，敵犯行在所，即取金部籍有關於國家經賦之大者載以行，及上於鎮江。

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial carriage to Weiyang, when the enemy struck the temporary palace he immediately took the Bureau of Finance registers relating to major state revenues and taxes and loaded them for travel, reaching Zhenjiang with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached Weiyang and the enemy attacked the temporary palace, he seized the Bureau of Finance registers bearing on major state revenues and carried them along, reaching Zhenjiang with the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時建炎三年二月也。

translations.literal: It was the second month of the third year of Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: This was the second month of Jianyan year 3.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂頤浩言於上，即日召見。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Lü Yihao spoke to the Emperor, and that same day Dai was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Lü Yihao spoke to the Emperor, and Dai was summoned that very day.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父喪，詔起復，以中散大夫直龍圖閣，為御營使司參議官兼措置軍前財用。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his father; an edict recalled him from mourning; as Gentleman for Promoting Culture with appointment at the Longtu Pavilion, he served as Planning Officer of the Imperial Camp Commissionerate and concurrently arranged front-line finances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he mourned his father, but an edict recalled him from mourning. As Gentleman for Promoting Culture with appointment at the Longtu Pavilion, he served as planning officer of the Imperial Camp Commissionerate and concurrently managed front-line finances.

sentences.zh: 苗傅、劉正彥叛，呂頤浩、張浚集勤王之師，迨流涕謂諸將曰：「君第行，無慮軍食。」

translations.literal: Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled; Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun gathered armies to rescue the throne. With tears Dai said to the generals: "You need only march—do not worry about provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun raised loyalist armies. Dai, weeping, told the generals: "March on—I will see to the food.

sentences.zh: 師行所至，食皆先具。

translations.literal: Wherever the army marched, food was prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the army went, provisions were already waiting.

sentences.zh: 事平，同趙哲等入對，上慰勞之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, together with Zhao Zhe and others he entered audience, and the Emperor comforted and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, he entered audience with Zhao Zhe and others, and the Emperor comforted and praised them.

sentences.zh: 詔轉三官，辭不拜，除權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered three ranks of promotion; he declined and did not accept; he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict offered him three ranks of promotion, but he declined; he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，加顯謨閣待制，為淮南、江、浙、荊湖等路制置發運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given the title Attendant Draftsman of the Xianmo Pavilion and made Commissioner for Circuit Transport Arrangement for Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, Jinghu, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Attendant Draftsman of the Xianmo Pavilion and Commissioner for Circuit Transport Arrangement for Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, Jinghu, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 尋以軍旅甫定，乞持餘服，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon, as the armies had only just settled, he begged to observe the remainder of mourning; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with the armies only just settled, he asked to complete the remainder of his mourning leave, and the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，知筠州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he was prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 2 he served as prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，移信州，尋提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Xinzhou; soon he was made commissioner of the Taiping Abbey at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Xinzhou, and soon afterward was made commissioner of the Taiping Abbey at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年十月，以舊職除兩浙路轉運使，言：「祖宗都大梁，歲漕東南六百餘萬斛，而六路之民無飛挽之擾，蓋所運者官舟，所役者兵卒故也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year he was reappointed by former rank as Transport Commissioner of the Two-Zhe Circuit and said: "Our founders made their capital at Daliang; each year more than six million hu were transported from the southeast, yet the people of the six circuits suffered no forced hauling—because official boats were used and soldier-bearers were employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year he was reappointed Transport Commissioner of the Two-Zhe Circuit and said: "When our founders held court at Daliang, over six million hu were shipped up from the southeast each year, yet the people of the six circuits were not dragooned for hauling—because the state used official boats and soldier-bearers.

sentences.zh: 今駐蹕浙右，漕運地裡不若中都之遠，而公私苦之，何也？

translations.literal: Now the court sojourns in western Zhe; the distance for grain transport is not as great as to the central capital, yet public and private both suffer—why?
translations.idiomatic: Now the court sojourns in western Zhe. The haul is shorter than to the old capital, yet everyone suffers—why?

sentences.zh: 以所用之舟太半取於民間，往往鑿井沉船以避其役。

translations.literal: Because more than half the boats used are taken from the populace; people often scuttle wells and sink boats to evade the corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Because more than half the boats are pressed from the people, who often scuttle wells and sink vessels to escape the levy.

sentences.zh: 如溫、明、虔、吉州等處所置造船場，乞委逐州守臣措置，募兵卒牽挽，使臣管押，庶幾害不及民，可以漸復漕運舊制。」

translations.literal: As for shipbuilding yards established at places such as Wen, Ming, Qian, and Jizhou, I ask that each prefecture's officials be charged to arrange them, recruit soldier-bearers for hauling, and have commissioners supervise transport—in this way harm may not reach the people, and the old grain-transport system may gradually be restored.
translations.idiomatic: For shipyards at Wen, Ming, Qian, Jizhou, and the like, I ask that each prefecture's officials be put in charge, soldier-bearers be recruited for hauling, and commissioners supervise transport—so the burden does not fall on the people and the old transport system can gradually be restored.

sentences.zh: 詔工部措置。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Works to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Works to take charge.

sentences.zh: 尋加徽猷閣直學士，升龍圖閣直學士，為四川都轉運使兼提舉成都等路茶事，並提舉陝西等路買馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion, promoted to Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, made Grand Transport Commissioner of Sichuan and concurrently Commissioner for Tea Affairs on the Chengdu and other circuits, and also Commissioner for Horse Purchases on the Shaanxi and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion, then promoted to Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, Grand Transport Commissioner of Sichuan, concurrently Commissioner for Tea Affairs on the Chengdu and other circuits, and Commissioner for Horse Purchases on the Shaanxi and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 自熙、豐以來，始即熙、秦、戎、黎等州置場買馬，而川茶通於永興四路，故成都府、秦州皆有榷茶司。

translations.literal: Since the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns, horse-buying stations had first been established at Xi, Qin, Rong, Li, and other prefectures; Sichuan tea circulated to the four Yongxing circuits; therefore both Chengdu Prefecture and Qinzhou had Tea Monopoly offices.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns, horse markets had been set up at Xi, Qin, Rong, Li, and other prefectures, and Sichuan tea flowed into the four Yongxing circuits—so both Chengdu Prefecture and Qinzhou had tea monopoly offices.

sentences.zh: 至是關陝既失，迨請合為一司，名都大提舉茶馬司，以省冗費，從之。

translations.literal: By this time Guan and Shaanxi had already been lost; Dai requested merging them into one office named the Grand Commissioner for Tea and Horses, to save redundant expense—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guan and Shaanxi had been lost. Dai asked that the offices be merged into one Grand Commissioner for Tea and Horses to cut waste, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，詔迨以每歲收支之數具旁通驛奏，迨乃考其本末，具奏曰：

translations.literal: After a year an edict ordered Dai to report yearly income and expenditure figures via express relay; Dai then examined causes and origins and submitted a detailed memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: A year later an edict required Dai to report annual receipts and expenditures by express relay. He traced the matter to its roots and submitted a detailed memorial:

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，所收錢物三千三百四十二萬餘緡，比所支闕五十一萬餘緡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, receipts in cash and goods totaled more than 33.42 million strings; compared with expenditures there was a shortfall of more than 510,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 4, receipts in cash and goods totaled more than 33.42 million strings, leaving a shortfall of more than 510,000 strings against expenditures.

sentences.zh: 五年，收三千六十萬緡，比所支闕一千萬餘緡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year receipts were 30.6 million strings; compared with expenditures there was a shortfall of more than 10 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 receipts were 30.6 million strings, with a shortfall of more than 10 million strings against expenditures.

sentences.zh: 六年，未見。

translations.literal: For the sixth year, no figures are yet available.
translations.idiomatic: For year 6, figures are not yet in.

sentences.zh: 七年，所收三千六百六十萬餘緡，比所支闕一百六十一萬餘緡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year receipts were more than 36.6 million strings; compared with expenditures there was a shortfall of more than 1.61 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 receipts exceeded 36.6 million strings, with a shortfall of more than 1.61 million strings against expenditures.

sentences.zh: 自來遇歲計有闕，即添支錢引補助。

translations.literal: Heretofore whenever the annual budget fell short, supplementary paper notes were printed to make up the deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the annual budget fell short, the practice has been to print supplementary paper notes to cover the gap.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，添印五百七十六萬道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, 5.76 million notes were additionally printed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 4, 5.76 million notes were additionally printed.

sentences.zh: 五年，添印二百萬道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, 2 million notes were additionally printed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, 2 million notes were additionally printed.

sentences.zh: 六年，添印六百萬道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, 6 million notes were additionally printed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, 6 million notes were additionally printed.

sentences.zh: 見今泛料太多，引價頓落，緣此未曾添印。

translations.literal: At present levies in kind are too numerous and note value has sharply fallen; for this reason no supplementary notes have been printed.
translations.idiomatic: Levies in kind are now excessive and note value has collapsed; for that reason no new notes have been printed.

sentences.zh: 兼歲收錢物內有上供、進奉等窠名一千五百九十九萬，系四川歲入舊額。

translations.literal: Moreover, within yearly receipts are categories such as tribute to the throne and presentation gifts totaling 15.99 million, being Sichuan's old annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Among annual receipts, categories such as tribute to the throne and presentation gifts total 15.99 million—the old Sichuan quota.

sentences.zh: 其勸諭、激賞等項窠名錢物共二千六十八萬，系軍興後來歲入所增，比舊額已過倍，其取於民可謂重矣。

translations.literal: Categories such as persuasion subsidies and merit rewards total 20.68 million, being increases to annual receipts after the military rising—more than double the old quota; what is taken from the people may be called heavy indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Categories such as persuasion subsidies and merit rewards total 20.68 million—postwar additions more than double the old quota. The burden on the people is plainly crushing.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗考《劉晏傳》，是時天下歲入緡錢千二百萬，而管榷居其半。

translations.literal: Your servant once examined the biography of Liu Yan: at that time the empire's annual receipts in cash strings totaled 12 million, and state monopolies accounted for half.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once studied the biography of Liu Yan. In his day the empire's annual cash receipts totaled 12 million strings, and state monopolies supplied half.

sentences.zh: 今四川榷鹽榷酒歲入一千九十一萬，過於晏所榷多矣。

translations.literal: Now Sichuan's salt and wine monopolies yield 10.91 million annually—already exceeding what Yan monopolized.
translations.idiomatic: Today Sichuan's salt and wine monopolies alone yield 10.91 million strings—more than Yan ever controlled.

sentences.zh: 諸窠名錢已三倍劉晏歲入之數，彼以一千二百萬贍中原之軍而有餘，今以三千六百萬貫贍川、陝一軍而不足。

translations.literal: All category receipts already triple Liu Yan's annual intake; he with 12 million supplied the armies of the Central Plain with surplus; now with 36 million strings we cannot supply one army in Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: All category receipts already triple Liu Yan's annual intake. He fed the armies of the Central Plain on 12 million strings with surplus; we cannot sustain one army in Sichuan and Shaanxi on 36 million.

sentences.zh: 又如折估及正色米一項，通計二百六十五萬石。

translations.literal: Again, items such as assessed conversion and standard-grade rice total 2.65 million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are assessed conversion and standard-grade rice, totaling 2.65 million shi.

sentences.zh: 止以紹興六年朝廷取會官兵數，計六萬八千四百四十九人，決無一年用二百六十五萬石米之理。

translations.literal: Based only on the civil and military roster the court compiled in the sixth year of Shaoxing—68,449 men in all—there is certainly no reason one year would require 2.65 million shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The court's Shaoxing year 6 roster lists only 68,449 civil and military personnel—there is no way one year requires 2.65 million shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 數內官員一萬一千七員，軍兵五萬七百四十九人，官員之數比軍兵之數約計六分之一。

translations.literal: Within the count are 11,017 officials and 50,749 soldiers; officials are roughly one-sixth the number of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, 11,017 are officials and 50,749 soldiers—officials are roughly one-sixth the number of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 軍兵請給錢比官員請給不及十分之一，即是冗濫在官員，不在軍兵也。

translations.literal: Soldiers' pay and allowances compared to officials' comprise less than one-tenth—thus redundancy is among officials, not soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' pay and allowances are less than one-tenth of officials'—the bloat is in the bureaucracy, not the ranks.

sentences.zh: 計司雖知冗濫，力不能裁節之，雖是寬剩，亦未敢除減，此朝廷不可不知也。

translations.literal: The fiscal offices though knowing the redundancy lack power to cut it; though there is surplus they dare not reduce—this the court must know.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal offices know the bloat but lack power to cut it; even where there is surplus they dare not trim—this the court must know.

sentences.zh: 蜀人所苦甚者，糴買、般運也。

translations.literal: What the people of Shu suffer most severely are grain purchases and transport.
translations.idiomatic: What the people of Shu suffer most are compulsory grain purchases and transport levies.

sentences.zh: 蓋糴買不科敷則不能集其事，苟科敷則不能無擾；

translations.literal: For grain purchase, without apportionment the task cannot be accomplished; yet if apportioned there cannot be no harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Grain purchases cannot be collected without apportionment, yet apportionment inevitably brings harassment.

sentences.zh: 般運事稍緩則船戶獨受其弊，急則稅戶皆被其害。

translations.literal: For transport, if the affair is slightly delayed boat households alone bear the harm; if urgent, all tax households suffer.
translations.idiomatic: If transport deadlines slip, boat households alone bear the cost; if they are rushed, every tax household suffers.

sentences.zh: 欲省漕運莫如屯田，漢中之地約收二十五萬餘石，若將一半充不系水運去處歲計米，以一半對減川路糴買、般發歲計米，亦可少寬民力。

translations.literal: To save on grain transport nothing surpasses frontier farming colonies; Hanzhong land yields about 250,000 shi; if half were used for annual grain quotas at places not dependent on water transport, and half used to offset Sichuan route purchase and transport quotas, the people's burden could be somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing saves transport costs like garrison farming. Hanzhong yields about 250,000 shi; if half supplied annual quotas at places not tied to waterways and half offset Sichuan purchase and transport quotas, the people's burden would ease somewhat.

sentences.zh: 兼臣已委官於興元、洋州就糴夏麥五十萬石，岷州欲就糴二十萬石，兼用營田所收一半之數十二萬石，三項共計五十七萬石。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has already commissioned officials at Xingyuan and Yangzhou to purchase 500,000 shi of summer wheat locally, wishes to purchase 200,000 shi locally at Minzhou, and together with half the garrison-farm harvest of 120,000 shi—the three items total 570,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has already sent officials to Xingyuan and Yangzhou to purchase 500,000 shi of summer wheat locally, plans 200,000 shi at Minzhou, and together with half the garrison-farm harvest—120,000 shi—the three items total 570,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 每年水運應付閬、利州以東計米五十八萬石，若得此三項，可盡數免川路糴買、般運，此乃恤民之實惠，守邊之良策也。

translations.literal: Each year water transport for points east of Lang and Lizhou requires 580,000 shi; with these three items the Sichuan route purchase and transport could be entirely waived—this is a real benefit to the people and a sound policy for defending the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Water transport east of Lang and Lizhou requires 580,000 shi each year. These three items would eliminate Sichuan purchase and transport entirely—a real relief for the people and a sound frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 降詔獎諭，以與吳玠不合，與祠。

translations.literal: An edict descended commending him; because he did not agree with Wu Jie, he was given a temple directorship.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him, but because he clashed with Wu Jie he was given a temple directorship.

sentences.zh: 九年，金人歸我三京，命迨為京畿都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Jin returned our three capitals; Dai was appointed Grand Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Jin returned the three capitals, Dai was appointed Grand Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 孟庾時為權東京留守，潛通北使。

translations.literal: Meng Yu at the time was Acting Commandant of the Eastern Capital, secretly communicating with northern envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yu was then Acting Commandant of the Eastern Capital, secretly in contact with northern envoys.

sentences.zh: 迨察其隱微，庾不能平，訟於朝，且使人告迨曰：「北人以兵至矣。」

translations.literal: Dai detected his hidden dealings; Yu could not be at peace, sued at court, and also sent someone to tell Dai: "The northerners have come with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dai uncovered his secret dealings. Yu, unable to contain himself, sued at court and sent a man to warn Dai: "The northerners are marching.

sentences.zh: 迨曰：「吾家食國家祿二百年，荷陛下重任，萬死不足報。

translations.literal: Dai said: "My family has eaten the state's salary for two hundred years; bearing Your Majesty's heavy trust, ten thousand deaths would not suffice to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: Dai replied: "My family has drawn the state's salary for two hundred years. Entrusted by Your Majesty with heavy responsibility, I could die ten thousand times and still not repay it.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣，豈能下穹廬之拜乎？

translations.literal: I am old—how could I bow beneath a felt tent?
translations.idiomatic: I am old. How could I bow beneath a felt tent?

sentences.zh: 首可斷而膝不可屈也。

translations.literal: My head may be severed but my knees cannot bend.
translations.idiomatic: My head may be cut off, but my knees will not bend.

sentences.zh: 如果然，吾將極罵以死。」

translations.literal: If it comes to that, I will revile them to the utmost and die.
translations.idiomatic: If it comes to that, I will curse them to the end and die.

sentences.zh: 告者悚然而去。

translations.literal: The informer, alarmed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 降聖節，庾失於行禮，為迨所持，庾自劾，迨因此求罷去，乃落職與祠歸，而庾以京師降于金人。

translations.literal: On the Descent of the Sage's Birthday festival Yu was remiss in ceremony; Dai seized on this; Yu impeached himself; Dai for this reason sought dismissal; he was demoted and given a temple directorship and sent home; Yu then surrendered the capital to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the Descent of the Sage's Birthday festival Yu botched the rites; Dai seized on the lapse. Yu impeached himself; Dai asked to be relieved, was demoted to a temple directorship, and sent home—after which Yu surrendered the capital to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 迨尋復龍圖閣待制、知洪州。

translations.literal: Soon Dai was restored as Attendant Draftsman of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Attendant Draftsman of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以疾丐祠。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, citing illness he begged for a temple directorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he pleaded illness and asked for a temple directorship.

sentences.zh: 十八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 趙開，字應祥，普州安居人。

translations.literal: Zhao Kai, style name Yingxiang, was a man of Anju in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kai, courtesy name Yingxiang, was a native of Anju in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 登元符三年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yuanfu year 3.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，權辟廱正。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan he was Acting Chief of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan year 2 he served as Acting Chief of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 用舉者改秩，即盡室如京師，買田尉氏，與四方賢俊遊，因詗知天下利病所當罷行者。

translations.literal: Through a recommender's nomination he changed rank; immediately he moved his whole household to the capital, bought land in Weishi, consorted with worthy men from all quarters, and thereby inquired into what throughout the empire should be abolished or implemented regarding benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for promotion, he moved his entire household to the capital, bought land in Weishi, and consorted with talented men from every quarter, learning what policies across the empire ought to be kept or scrapped.

sentences.zh: 如是七年，慨然有通變救弊志。

translations.literal: Thus for seven years he was stirred with resolve to adapt and remedy abuses.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years he nursed a resolve to reform what was broken.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，除禮制局校正檢閱官。

translations.literal: Early in Xuanhe he was appointed Collator and Inspector of the Rites Regulations Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe era he was appointed Collator and Inspector of the Rites Regulations Bureau.

sentences.zh: 數月局罷，出知鄢陵縣。

translations.literal: After several months the bureau was abolished; he went out as magistrate of Yanling County.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later the bureau was abolished, and he was sent out as magistrate of Yanling County.

sentences.zh: 七年，除講議司檢詳官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Examining Officer of the Policy Discussion Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Examining Officer of the Policy Discussion Office.

sentences.zh: 開善心計，自檢詳罷，除成都路轉運判官，遂奏罷宣和六年所增上供認額綱布十萬匹，減綿州下戶支移利州水腳錢十分之三，又減蒲江六井元符至宣和所增鹽額，列其次第，謂之「鼠尾帳」，揭示鄉戶歲時所當輸折科等實數，俾人人具曉，鄉胥不得隱匿竄寄。

translations.literal: Kai was skilled at fiscal calculation. After his examiner post was abolished, he was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of the Chengdu Circuit. He then memorialized to abolish the 100,000 bolts of tribute cloth added in Xuanhe year 6, reduced by three-tenths the water-transport fees that lower households in Mianzhou had to pay when reassigned to Lizhou, and also reduced the salt quotas added at Pujiang's Six Wells from Yuanfu through Xuanhe. He listed these in order, calling it the "Mouse-Tail Ledger," posting the actual amounts households in townships were to pay in annual assessed levies so everyone would fully understand and village clerks could not conceal or shift registrations.
translations.idiomatic: Kai had a gift for fiscal affairs. After his examiner post ended, he became Transport Vice Commissioner of the Chengdu Circuit. He memorialized to abolish the 100,000 bolts of tribute cloth added in Xuanhe year 6, cut by three-tenths the water-transport fees lower households in Mianzhou paid when reassigned to Lizhou, and rolled back salt quotas added at Pujiang's Six Wells from Yuanfu through Xuanhe. Listing these in order, he called the register the "Mouse-Tail Ledger," posting the actual levies each township owed so every household would know and village clerks could not conceal or shift the burden.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「財利之源當出於一，祖宗朝天下財計盡歸三司，諸道利源各歸漕計，故官省事理。

translations.literal: He once said: "The sources of revenue ought to issue from one place; in the founders' reign all the empire's fiscal affairs were gathered in the Three Departments, and each circuit's revenue sources returned to transport commissioners—therefore government was lean and affairs clear.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Revenue ought to flow through a single channel. Under the founders, all fiscal affairs went to the Three Departments and each circuit's revenues to its transport commissioner—government was lean and affairs clear.

sentences.zh: 並廢以還，漕司則利害可以參究，而無牽掣窒礙之患矣。」

translations.literal: Abolish the separate offices and restore this, and the transport commissioners can weigh benefit and harm together, without the affliction of mutual obstruction and deadlock.
translations.idiomatic: Restore that system and transport commissioners can weigh costs and benefits without the tangles and deadlocks of divided authority.

sentences.zh: 因指陳榷茶、買馬五害，大略謂：「黎州買馬，嘉祐歲額才二千一百餘。

translations.literal: He then set forth the five harms of the tea monopoly and horse purchases, saying in general: "At Lizhou horse purchases, the Jiayou annual quota was only a little over 2,100.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out five harms of the tea monopoly and horse trade, saying in brief: "At Lizhou, the Jiayou quota was barely 2,100 horses.

sentences.zh: 自置司榷茶，歲額四千，且獲馬兵逾千人，猶不足用，多費衣糧，為一害。

translations.literal: Since establishing the tea monopoly office the annual quota is 4,000, and though more than a thousand horse soldiers are obtained, it is still insufficient; much clothing and grain is wasted—the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: Since the monopoly office was set up the quota is 4,000, and even with more than a thousand horse soldiers it is still not enough—yet clothing and grain pour out in waste. That is the first harm.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐以銀絹博馬，價皆有定。

translations.literal: Under Jiayou silver and silk were exchanged for horses at fixed prices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiayou, horses were bought with silver and silk at fixed prices.

sentences.zh: 今長吏旁緣為奸，不時歸貨，以空券給夷人，使待資次，夷人怨恨，必生邊患，為二害。

translations.literal: Now local officials exploit the margins for fraud, do not return goods on schedule, and give empty vouchers to the barbarians, making them wait their turn; the barbarians resent this and border trouble will surely arise—the second harm.
translations.idiomatic: Today local officials twist the rules, fail to deliver goods on time, and pay the tribes with empty vouchers, making them wait their turn. Resentment breeds border trouble—the second harm.

sentences.zh: 初置司榷茶，借本錢于轉運司五十二萬緡，于常平司二十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: When the tea monopoly office was first established it borrowed capital of 520,000 strings from the transport commissionerate and more than 200,000 strings from the Ever-Normal Granary office.
translations.idiomatic: When the monopoly office was first set up it borrowed 520,000 strings from the transport commissionerate and more than 200,000 from the Ever-Normal Granary office.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧至今幾六十年，舊所借不償一文，而歲借乃准初數，為三害。

translations.literal: From Xining to the present is nearly sixty years; not one cash of the original loans has been repaid, yet each year new loans match the original amounts—the third harm.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly sixty years have passed since Xining, yet not one cash of the original loans has been repaid—while fresh loans match the original sums each year. That is the third harm.

sentences.zh: 榷茶之初，預俵茶戶本錢，尋於數外更增和買，或遂抑預俵錢充和買，茶戶坐是破產，而官買歲增。

translations.literal: At the start of the tea monopoly, advance capital was distributed to tea households; soon compulsory purchases beyond the quota were added, or advance funds were seized to meet compulsory purchases; tea households for this reason went bankrupt while official purchases rose year by year.
translations.idiomatic: At first advance capital went to tea households; soon compulsory purchases beyond quota were added, or advance funds were seized to meet them. Tea households went bankrupt while official purchases climbed year by year.

sentences.zh: 茶日濫雜，官茶既不堪食，則私販公行，刑不能禁，為四害。

translations.literal: Tea grew daily more adulterated; once official tea was unfit to eat, private smuggling flourished openly and punishment could not stop it—the fourth harm.
translations.idiomatic: Tea grew ever more adulterated; official tea became inedible, private trade flourished openly, and punishment could not stop it—the fourth harm.

sentences.zh: 承平時，蜀茶之入秦者十幾八九，猶患積壓難售。

translations.literal: In peaceful times eight or nine tenths of Shu tea entered Qin, yet there was still worry over backlog and difficulty in selling.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peaceful times eight or nine tenths of Shu tea went to Qin, and still piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 今關、隴悉遭焚蕩，仍拘舊額，竟何所用？

translations.literal: Now Guan and Long have been burned bare, yet the old quotas are still enforced—what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: Now Guan and Long lie in ashes, yet old quotas are enforced—to what end?

sentences.zh: 茶兵官吏坐縻衣糧，未免科配州縣，為五害。

translations.literal: Tea soldiers and officials sit consuming clothing and grain and inevitably levy assessments on prefectures and counties—the fifth harm.
translations.idiomatic: Tea soldiers and officials consume clothing and grain without end and inevitably levy assessments on prefectures and counties—the fifth harm.

sentences.zh: 請依嘉祐故事，盡罷榷茶，仍令轉運司買馬，即五害並去，而邊患不生。

translations.literal: I ask that following the Jiayou precedent the tea monopoly be entirely abolished and horse purchases be returned to the transport commissionerate; then all five harms would be removed and border trouble would not arise.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we follow the Jiayou precedent, abolish the tea monopoly entirely, and return horse purchases to the transport commissionerate—all five harms gone, and no border trouble.

sentences.zh: 如謂榷茶未可遽罷，亦宜並歸轉運司，痛減額以蘇茶戶，輕立價以惠茶商，如此則私販必衰，盜賊消弭，本錢既常在，而息錢自足。」

translations.literal: If one says the tea monopoly cannot be abruptly abolished, it should still be merged under the transport commissionerate, quotas sharply cut to revive tea households, prices lightly set to benefit tea merchants—then private smuggling will surely decline, bandits will be pacified, capital will always be on hand, and interest will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If the monopoly cannot be abolished at once, it should still be merged under the transport commissionerate: slash quotas to revive tea households, set fair prices to help merchants—then smuggling will fade, bandits subside, capital will stay in place, and interest will suffice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷是其言，即擢開都大提舉川、陝茶馬事，使推行之。

translations.literal: The court approved his words and immediately promoted Kai to Grand Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi Tea and Horse Affairs, ordering him to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and immediately promoted Kai to Grand Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi Tea and Horse Affairs to carry the reforms out.

sentences.zh: 時建炎二年也。

translations.literal: It was the second year of Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: This was Jianyan year 2.

sentences.zh: 於是大更茶馬之法，官買官賣茶並罷，參酌政和二年東京都茶務所創條約，印給茶引，使茶商執引與茶戶自相貿易。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tea-and-horse system was greatly changed; official purchase and sale of tea were both abolished; adapting the regulations created in the second year of Zhenghe by the Eastern Capital Tea Bureau, tea certificates were printed and issued, allowing tea merchants bearing certificates to trade directly with tea households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the tea-and-horse system was overhauled: official purchase and sale of tea were abolished. Adapting regulations from the Eastern Capital Tea Bureau in Zhenghe year 2, the state printed tea certificates so merchants could trade directly with tea households.

sentences.zh: 改成都舊買賣茶場為合同場買引所，仍于合同場置茶市，交易者必由市，引與茶必相隨。

translations.literal: The old Chengdu tea buying-and-selling yards were changed to contract-yard certificate offices; tea markets were still set at the contract yards—traders had to go through the market, and certificate and tea had to go together.
translations.idiomatic: The old Chengdu tea buying-and-selling yards were changed to contract-yard certificate offices; tea markets were still set at the contract yards—traders had to go through the market, and certificate and tea had to go together.

sentences.zh: 茶戶十或十五共為一保，並籍定茶鋪姓名，互察影帶販鬻者。

translations.literal: Tea households formed mutual-security groups of ten or fifteen, with tea-shop names registered, mutually watching for covert trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: Tea households formed mutual-security groups of ten or fifteen, with tea-shop names registered, mutually watching for covert trafficking.

sentences.zh: 凡買茶引，每一斤春為錢七十，夏五十，舊所輸市例頭子錢並依舊。

translations.literal: For each certificate purchased, spring tea was seventy cash per jin, summer fifty; the old market head-money payments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For each certificate purchased, spring tea was seventy cash per jin, summer fifty; the old market head-money payments remained as before.

sentences.zh: 茶所過每一斤徵一錢，住徵一錢半。

translations.literal: At each tea station one cash per jin was levied in transit; at destination one and a half cash.
translations.idiomatic: At each tea station one cash per jin was levied in transit; at destination one and a half cash.

sentences.zh: 其合同場監官除驗引、秤茶、封記、發放外，無得干預茶商、茶戶交易事。

translations.literal: Contract-yard supervisors, apart from verifying certificates, weighing tea, sealing marks, and issuing release, might not interfere in dealings between tea merchants and tea households.
translations.idiomatic: Contract-yard supervisors, apart from verifying certificates, weighing tea, sealing marks, and issuing release, might not interfere in dealings between tea merchants and tea households.

sentences.zh: 舊制買馬及三千匹者轉一官，比但以所買數推賞，往往有一任轉數官者。

translations.literal: Under the old system buying three thousand horses earned one rank promotion; recently rewards were reckoned only by numbers bought, and often one tenure brought several promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system buying three thousand horses earned one rank promotion; recently rewards were reckoned only by numbers bought, and often one tenure brought several promotions.

sentences.zh: 開奏：「請推賞必以馬到京實收數為格，或死於道，黜降有差。」

translations.literal: Kai memorialized: "I ask that rewards be measured strictly by horses actually received in the capital; if they die on the road, demotions should differ in degree."
translations.idiomatic: Kai memorialized, "I ask that rewards be measured strictly by horses actually received in the capital; if they die on the road, demotions should differ in degree."

sentences.zh: 比及四年冬，茶引收息至一百七十餘萬緡，買馬乃逾二萬匹。

translations.literal: By the fourth winter, tea-certificate interest reached more than 1.7 million strings, and horses bought exceeded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth winter, tea-certificate interest reached more than 1.7 million strings, and horses bought exceeded twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 張浚以知樞密院宣撫川蜀，素知開善理財，即承制以開兼宣撫處置使司隨軍轉運使，專一總領四川財賦。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with authority to pacify Sichuan, knew Kai was skilled at managing finances and by special order made Kai concurrently army-follow transport commissioner of the Pacification headquarters, solely in charge of Sichuan's revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with authority to pacify Sichuan, knew Kai was skilled at managing finances and by special order made Kai concurrently army-follow transport commissioner of the Pacification headquarters, solely in charge of Sichuan's revenues.

sentences.zh: 開見浚曰：「蜀之民力盡矣，錙銖不可加，獨榷貨稍存贏餘，而貪猾認為己有，互相隱匿。

translations.literal: Kai, meeting Jun, said: "Shu's manpower is exhausted—not a cash can be added; only monopoly goods still show some surplus, yet the greedy claim it as their own and hide it from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, meeting Jun, said, "Shu's manpower is exhausted—not a cash can be added; only monopoly goods still show some surplus, yet the greedy claim it as their own and hide it from each other.

sentences.zh: 惟不恤怨詈，斷而敢行，庶可救一時之急。」

translations.literal: Only by not fearing curses and acting decisively can we perhaps relieve the urgent moment."
translations.idiomatic: Only by not fearing curses and acting decisively can we perhaps relieve the urgent moment."

sentences.zh: 浚銳意興復，委任不疑，於是大變酒法，自成都始。

translations.literal: Jun was keen to restore the realm and entrusted him without doubt; thereupon the wine law was greatly changed, beginning at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was keen to restore the realm and entrusted him without doubt; thereupon the wine law was greatly changed, beginning at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先罷公使賣供給酒，即舊撲買坊場所置隔槽，設官主之，曲與釀具官悉自買，聽釀戶各以米赴官場自釀，凡一石米輸三千，並頭子雜用等二十二。

translations.literal: First the envoy-sale of supply wine was abolished; at the old licensed brewery sites partitioned troughs were set up under official management; yeast and brewing equipment were all bought by the office; brewers might bring grain to the government yard and brew themselves—for each shi of grain they paid three thousand cash, plus twenty-two items of head-money and miscellaneous dues.
translations.idiomatic: First the envoy-sale of supply wine was abolished; at the old licensed brewery sites partitioned troughs were set up under official management; yeast and brewing equipment were all bought by the office; brewers might bring grain to the government yard and brew themselves—for each shi of grain they paid three thousand cash, plus twenty-two items of head-money and miscellaneous dues.

sentences.zh: 其釀之多寡，惟錢是視，不限數也。

translations.literal: How much they brewed depended only on money paid—there was no limit on quantity.
translations.idiomatic: How much they brewed depended only on money paid—there was no limit on quantity.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂遍四路行其法。

translations.literal: The next year the method was extended through all four circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the method was extended through all four circuits.

sentences.zh: 又法成都府法，于秦州置錢引務，興州鼓鑄銅錢，官賣銀絹，聽民以錢引或銅錢買之。

translations.literal: Following the Chengdu model, a note office was set up at Qin Prefecture; at Xing Prefecture copper cash was cast; the state sold silk and silver, allowing the people to buy with cash notes or copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Chengdu model, a note office was set up at Qin Prefecture; at Xing Prefecture copper cash was cast; the state sold silk and silver, allowing the people to buy with cash notes or copper coins.

sentences.zh: 凡民錢當入官者，並聽用引折納，官支出亦如之。

translations.literal: All money the people owed the state might be paid in notes at discount; state payments likewise.
translations.idiomatic: All money the people owed the state might be paid in notes at discount; state payments likewise.

sentences.zh: 民私用引為市，於一千並五百上許從便增高其直，惟不得減削。

translations.literal: The people might use notes privately in trade; on denominations of one thousand and five hundred they might raise the rate as convenient, but not reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: The people might use notes privately in trade; on denominations of one thousand and five hundred they might raise the rate as convenient, but not reduce it.

sentences.zh: 法既流通，民以為便。

translations.literal: Once the law circulated, the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Once the law circulated, the people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 初，錢引兩料通行才二百五十萬有奇，至是添印至四千一百九十餘萬，人亦不厭其多，價亦不削。

translations.literal: At first only about 2.5 million strings of the two note issues circulated; now printing was increased to more than 41.9 million—yet people did not resent the abundance, nor did value fall.
translations.idiomatic: At first only about 2.5 million strings of the two note issues circulated; now printing was increased to more than 41.9 million—yet people did not resent the abundance, nor did value fall.

sentences.zh: 宣司獲偽引三十萬，盜五十人，浚欲從有司議當以死，開白浚曰：「相君誤矣。

translations.literal: The Pacification headquarters seized three hundred thousand counterfeit notes and fifty counterfeiters; Jun wished to follow the regular offices and sentence them to death; Kai told Jun: "My lord is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification headquarters seized three hundred thousand counterfeit notes and fifty counterfeiters; Jun wished to follow the regular offices and sentence them to death; Kai told Jun, "My lord is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 使引偽，加宣撫使印其上即為真。

translations.literal: If the notes are false, stamp the Pacification commissioner's seal on them and they become genuine.
translations.idiomatic: If the notes are false, stamp the Pacification commissioner's seal on them and they become genuine.

sentences.zh: 黥其徒使治幣，是相君一日獲三十萬之錢，而起五十人之死也。」

translations.literal: Brand the men and make them mint coin—in one day my lord gains three hundred thousand in cash while sparing fifty lives."
translations.idiomatic: Brand the men and make them mint coin—in one day my lord gains three hundred thousand in cash while sparing fifty lives."

sentences.zh: 浚稱善，悉如開言。

translations.literal: Jun approved and did all as Kai said.
translations.idiomatic: Jun approved and did all as Kai said.

sentences.zh: 最後又變鹽法，其法實視大觀東南、東北鹽鈔條約，置合同場鹽市，與茶法大抵相類。

translations.literal: Finally the salt law was changed again; the method in fact followed the Daguan salt-certificate treaties of southeast and northeast, setting contract-yard salt markets broadly like the tea law.
translations.idiomatic: Finally the salt law was changed again; the method in fact followed the Daguan salt-certificate treaties of southeast and northeast, setting contract-yard salt markets broadly like the tea law.

sentences.zh: 鹽引每一斤納錢二十五，土產稅有增添等共納九錢四分，所過每斤徵錢七分，住徵一錢五分，若以錢引折納，別輸稱提勘合錢共六十。

translations.literal: Each salt certificate paid twenty-five cash per jin; local-product taxes and additions totaled nine cash four fen; transit levied seven cash per jin, destination one and a half cash; if paid in cash notes, a separate weighing-and-verification fee of sixty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each salt certificate paid twenty-five cash per jin; local-product taxes and additions totaled nine cash four fen; transit levied seven cash per jin, destination one and a half cash; if paid in cash notes, a separate weighing-and-verification fee of sixty in all.

sentences.zh: 初變榷法，怨詈四起，至是開覆議更鹽法，言者遂奏其不便，乞罷之以安遠民，且曰：「如謂大臣建請，務全事體，必須更制，即乞劄與張浚照會。」

translations.literal: When the monopoly law was first changed, curses rose on every side; when Kai again debated revising the salt law, critics memorialized its inconvenience and begged to abolish it to settle distant peoples, saying: "If great ministers initiated it and the whole affair must be preserved, and reform is required, then please send a directive to Zhang Jun for coordination."
translations.idiomatic: When the monopoly law was first changed, curses rose on every side; when Kai again debated revising the salt law, critics memorialized its inconvenience and begged to abolish it to settle distant peoples, saying, "If great ministers initiated it and the whole affair must be preserved, and reform is required, then please send a directive to Zhang Jun for coordination."

sentences.zh: 詔以其章示浚，浚不為變。

translations.literal: An edict showed the memorial to Jun; Jun made no change.
translations.idiomatic: An edict showed the memorial to Jun; Jun made no change.

sentences.zh: 時浚荷重寄，治兵秦川，經營兩河，旬犒月賞，期得士死力，費用不貲，盡取辦於開，開悉知慮於食貨，算無遺策，雖支費不可計，而贏貲若有餘。

translations.literal: At the time Jun bore heavy trust, drilled troops in Qin-chuan, and planned the two Rivers; ten-day rewards and monthly bonuses sought to make soldiers die with all their strength—expense beyond reckoning, all provided by Kai; Kai understood food and goods thoroughly, his calculations leaving nothing out; though disbursements could not be counted, surplus seemed always at hand.
